# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations

What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
the current code (not just the older audit notes).

How this file relates to the others:

- `docs/TODO.md` - the engineering fix backlog (failure modes `F-T*`). It is
  the *plan to fix*. This file is the *plain-English "do not do this" list*.
- `ROADMAP.md` - feature roadmap. Its bug-audit wave `B1-B20` is fully closed,
  so those are NOT limitations anymore. The open items live in `docs/TODO.md`.

Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.

---

## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow

This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
consequence of it.

When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.

So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
be:

- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
- No system calls / semihosting
- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)

If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.

---

## State coverage: what the wire format carries

Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`), and the QEMU2 handback
(`tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`).

### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`

- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed

### NOT in the wire format at all

- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.

### Carried but NOT restored into vsim

The struct holds them so they survive QEMU1 -> QEMU2, but `ResumeDriver`
writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:

- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).

Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`).

### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free

Four surfaces, four ceilings:

| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |
| QEMU2 handback  | gdbstub P-packet by NAME                      | silently skipped if stub omits the name (L16); `vl / vtype` already needed a QEMU fork patch |

Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":

1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
   the cycle figure.

Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).

---

## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload

### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)

- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.

### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)

- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
  the vsim window only.)
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
- Status: OPEN.

### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI

- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
  almost anything under an OS.
- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
  `resume()` never writes it.
- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
  PMP-static but not paging).

### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)

- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
  the ROI starts from reset values.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
- Status: OPEN.

### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)

- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
  at the trigger.

### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
  it, while running FP code inside.
- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
  reset value (RNE, no flags); QEMU2 keeps QEMU1's pre-trigger value
  with no sync. FP results inside the ROI use the wrong rounding;
  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
  enabled, drain before handback.

---

## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up

### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)

- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
  trigger boundary.
- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
- Status: OPEN.

### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)

- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
  shared memory.
- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
  corruption.
- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
  ELF size against it.
- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.

### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)

- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
  sync.
- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
  both.
- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)

- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
  any aliased/device memory.
- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
  device state then disagrees with vsim.
- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
- Status: OPEN.

---

## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. The whole pipeline is hard-wired to one CPU

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU other than
  `andes-ax45mpv`, or any VLEN other than 512.
- What happens: the QEMU2 spawn passes `-machine andes_ae350` and
  `-cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512` literally (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`).
  The V-register scratch address is the constant `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000`
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:42`), which is only correct when RAM base is 0 (true
  for `andes_ae350`, wrong for `-M virt` where it would need 0x80FF0000).
  The shared-memory base defaults to 0 in `spawn.py`. Nothing parameterizes
  these per machine.
- Where: `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp:38-42`.
- Status: by design for now; blocks porting to another core.

### L11. VLEN is fixed at 512 bits, and a mismatch is silent  (F-T3.4)

- When it bites: a fixture built for a different VLEN than the vsim config,
  or any future config change to VLEN.
- What happens: the wire format reserves 64 bytes per vector register
  (`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 64`, `state_abi.h:34`). There is no runtime check
  that `vlenb` from QEMU equals `vlenb` in vsim. If they differ, the upper
  bytes of each V register are uninitialized scratch -> garbage in the V
  regfile. The constant is also duplicated in `checkpoint.py:44`
  (`LIVE_VLEN_BYTES = 64`) and can drift from `spawn.py`.
- Where: `state_abi.h:34`, `v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `checkpoint.py:44`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L12. CSR-mode trigger collides with real use of CSR 0x7C0

- When it bites: a workload that legitimately writes CSR `0x7C0` with
  immediate 0 or 1.
- What happens: the default (CSR) mode treats `csrwi 0x7C0, 0` as ROI entry
  and `csrwi 0x7C0, 1` as exit. A real write to that CSR would false-trigger
  a handoff. (0x7C0 is a benign vendor CSR on ax45mp, so this is unlikely in
  practice, but it is a hard assumption.)
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` CSR matcher; `csr_trigger.hpp`.
- Status: inherent to CSR mode. Workaround: use `--mode pc` or `--mode icount`.

### L13. CSR marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18, documented)

- When it bites: never today, but worth knowing.
- What happens: the matcher skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:505-506`). RV32C has no compressed `csrwi`, so this is
  correct now; if a future extension adds a 16-bit CSR write the marker and
  this gate must change together.
- Where: `hybrid_handoff.c:499-506`.
- Status: documented limit, no action needed now.

### L14. The SimPoint cycle estimate is an approximation, not a measurement

- When it bites: any `--mode simpoint` / `./hsim estimate` run where you read
  the headline `estimated_cycles` as if it were exact.
- What happens: each phase CPI is sampled from a single window of
  `vsim_icount` instructions at the slice boundary
  (`hsim:1188-1193`), and the whole-program figure is
  `N_total * weighted_CPI`. Two accuracy gaps:
  1. The microarchitectural state (caches, branch predictor) is cold at each
     window start unless you pass `--vsim-warmup-icount`. Without warmup the
     CPI is biased high.
  2. No error bound or confidence interval is reported. The estimate inherits
     SimPoint's usual phase-approximation error.
- Where: `hsim:1122-1202` (`_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: by design; mitigate with `--vsim-warmup-icount`.

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are not transported  (new 2026-05-28)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: zero Andes vendor CSRs appear in `hybrid_state_v1`;
  none are drained, restored, or read back. vsim runs the ROI with
  whatever its reset / boot-time values were. Cache-enable, prefetcher,
  branch-predictor, and ECC controls in particular shape the cycle
  count, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only a correctness one.
  CSR `0x7C0` is also actively repurposed by the trigger matcher (L12)
  instead of being preserved.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no Andes block);
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no Andes handles);
  `resume_driver.hpp` (no Andes restore path).
- Status: OPEN. Any v2 extension should label each Andes CSR as either
  microarch-only (read-only / boot-set, no runtime restore needed) or
  software-visible (must round-trip).

---

## Tier 4 - Robustness and tooling gaps

### L15. No value-level check that the handoff copied state correctly  (F-T3.1)

- When it bites: any bug that copies the wrong register, byte-swaps, or
  truncates a 64-bit value in the icount or simpoint paths.
- What happens: those paths only assert exit code and PC range. A wrong
  register value passes silently. There is no `g`-packet readback compared
  against the drained state.
- Where: `hsim` (`_run_drain_pair`, `_run_simpoint_pipeline`).
- Status: OPEN. This is the cheapest high-value fix (see TODO.md "next moves").

### L16. CSR restore to QEMU2 is silently skipped if the stub omits the name

- When it bites: a QEMU build whose feature XML does not advertise some CSR
  (e.g. `medeleg`, `satp`, `mie`).
- What happens: GPRs and PC hard-fail if missing, but every CSR/PMP/V write
  goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns quietly when the name is not
  found (`gdbstub.py:251-258`). That CSR keeps QEMU2's reset value with no
  warning. The asymmetry (hard-fail GPR vs silent-skip CSR) is the hazard.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:251-258`, used at `gdbstub.py:299-305`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L17. gdbstub handback uses a fixed 10 s timeout and a racy port pick

- When it bites: QEMU2 slow to answer under host load; or many parallel runs
  (the `JOBS=8` e2e runner) picking ports at the same time.
- What happens: `RECV_TIMEOUT = 10.0` is hardcoded (`gdbstub.py:135`); a slow
  reply raises mid-restore and the run dies. `pick_free_port` binds port 0,
  reads the number, closes, then QEMU binds it later - a TOCTOU window where
  another process can grab the port (`spawn.py`, acknowledged in its
  comment). Wrong-port connect = hang until timeout.
- Where: `gdbstub.py:135`, `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py`.
- Status: OPEN.

### L18. Wire format is little-endian / same-arch only

- When it bites: running any component on a big-endian host, or mixing hosts
  with different struct alignment.
- What happens: the state struct is exchanged byte-for-byte with no byte-swap
  path (`state_abi.h:7-9`). The Python mirror uses a native-endian
  `ctypes.Structure` (`abi.py:30`), so a BE host would mis-parse the body
  while the `<II` magic check still passes - a silent mis-read.
- Where: `state_abi.h:7-9`, `abi.py:30`.
- Status: by design (x86-64 host + RV64 guest only).

### L19. Other un-guarded failure paths  (F-T3.3, F-T3.5, F-T3.6, F-T3.8)

- Determinism is not guaranteed across re-runs (reserved bytes, CSR drain
  order); no test pins byte-identical output.
- Submodule version drift (QEMU plugin ABI, vsim DM, pinned SimPoint
  `17783e5`) has no CI gate.
- Failure injection is thin: partial drain, disk full, mmap truncated
  mid-run are not covered.
- A QEMU2 that launches but never answers the gdbstub can be left as a
  zombie (no SIGALRM watchdog around the handshake).
- Status: all OPEN, lower priority.

---

## Documentation drift (not a runtime limit, but a trap)

`CLAUDE.md` and parts of the architecture notes still describe
`verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp` as the component that spawns QEMU2
and sends gdbstub P-packets. That file no longer exists - the QEMU2 spawn and
handback moved into the Python orchestrator (`tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` +
`gdbstub.py`) in commit `7c7bf30`. Anyone debugging the handback by following
the docs will look in the wrong place.

---

## Quick reference

| ID  | Limitation                              | Severity | Status |
|-----|-----------------------------------------|----------|--------|
| L1  | No syscalls/semihosting in ROI          | blocker  | open   |
| L2  | PMP not restored to vsim                | high     | open   |
| L3  | Paging (satp) off in ROI                | high     | open   |
| L4  | Trap state lost across ROI              | high     | open   |
| L5  | LR/SC cannot cross handoff              | high     | open   |
| L6  | Privilege forced to M-mode              | high     | open   |
| L7  | 128 MB mmap, no bounds check            | medium   | open   |
| L8  | Single hart only                        | medium   | open   |
| L9  | MMIO in ROI not handled                 | medium   | open   |
| L10 | Hard-wired to andes_ae350 / ax45mpv     | medium   | by design |
| L11 | VLEN fixed at 512, mismatch silent      | medium   | open   |
| L12 | CSR 0x7C0 trigger collision             | low      | inherent |
| L13 | CSR marker must be 32-bit               | low      | documented |
| L14 | SimPoint estimate is approximate        | medium   | by design |
| L15 | No value-level handoff check            | medium   | open   |
| L16 | CSR restore silently skipped if missing | medium   | open   |
| L17 | Fixed gdbstub timeout + racy port       | low      | open   |
| L18 | Little-endian / same-arch only          | low      | by design |
| L19 | Determinism / drift / fault-injection   | low      | open   |
| L20 | fcsr/frm/fflags not transported         | high     | open   |
| L21 | Andes vendor CSRs not transported       | high     | open   |

---

## Commercial product quality rating  (assessed 2026-05-28)

Honest scorecard for "is this a shippable commercial product today?".
Rated against industry baselines (Synopsys VCS, Cadence Xcelium,
gem5 + functional warmup) for a CPU vendor's hybrid sim offering.

**Overall: 4/10 as a shippable commercial product. ~7/10 as an internal
/ research tool inside its narrow design envelope.**

### Axis breakdown

| Axis                                  | Score | Note |
|---------------------------------------|-------|------|
| Architecture clarity                  | 8/10  | Three-phase handoff is clean; shared ABI is a single header. |
| Engineering discipline                | 7/10  | TDD gate, doctest, parallel CI, candid `limitation.md`. |
| State coverage (correctness surface)  | 3/10  | 21 documented limitations; only 4 CSRs round-trip into vsim. |
| Generality of workload                | 2/10  | ROI must be M-mode, trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls (L1-L6). |
| ISA completeness                      | 3/10  | No S/U mode, no fcsr, no HPM, zero Andes vendor CSRs (vendor IS Andes). |
| Wire-format extensibility             | 4/10  | v1 only; growth happens by carving `reserved[216]` ad-hoc. No v2 path. |
| Robustness / errors                   | 5/10  | `cmderr` is cleared and swallowed; only a private diagnostic side channel. |
| Docs / onboarding                     | 7/10  | `CLAUDE.md`, `USER_GUIDE.md`, `limitation.md` are unusually honest. |
| Test fixtures                         | 6/10  | Solid asm + C-runtime e2e, but no OS-mode, no FP-rounding, no trap fixtures. |
| Portability                           | 4/10  | x86-64 host + little-endian assumed (L18); pinned Andes toolchain; podman-only vsim build. |

### What blocks commercial shipping

1. **Silent correctness gaps.** `fcsr/frm/fflags` never round-trip (L20)
   - an FP workload that touches rounding mode will look numerically
   fine but be wrong. `cmderr` is W1C-cleared so a partial CSR restore
   is observable only through a private counter
   (`resume_driver.hpp:196-205`).
2. **ROI envelope is too narrow.** "M-mode only, no traps, no paging,
   no syscalls inside the window" (L1-L6) rules out every real
   OS-bearing benchmark - SPEC under Linux, any driver code, anything
   with page faults.
3. **No Andes vendor CSRs.** For an Andes product, shipping zero
   `mmsc_cfg / mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` transport (L21) is a
   credibility hit and an accuracy hazard - cache and prefetcher
   controls shape the cycle count.
4. **Only 4 CSRs restored into vsim.** `satp`, `mepc/mcause/mtval`,
   `mscratch`, `mip/mie`, PMP are drained but never written back into
   vsim (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`). They exist in the wire format
   but not in the simulator. Any future need for traps or dynamic
   PMP needs `resume_driver` extended.
5. **Wire format is v1-locked with ad-hoc growth.** Each new field
   steals from `reserved[]` (warmup metadata already ate 16 bytes;
   `state_abi.h:85-88`). No deprecation path, no feature bits beyond
   the three `HYBRID_FLAG_*` bits.
6. **Build/test infrastructure is single-host.** Podman-required vsim
   build, hardcoded `JOBS=8` ceiling on 128-core hosts,
   `/dev/shm`-backed fixtures - all fine for a lab, painful for a
   commercial CI matrix.

### What it does well (the 7/10 internal-tool score)

- Three-phase handoff is a clear, documented contract.
- `state_abi.h` plus `static_assert`s pin layout - good ABI hygiene.
- The team writes down what does NOT work (this file, 21 entries plus
  the state-coverage section) instead of hiding it. Commercially that
  is the release-blocker checklist; internally it is exemplary.
- SimPoint integration for whole-program cycle estimation (L14) is a
  real differentiator over a pure functional sim.

### Bottom line

Ship-grade architecture, research-grade coverage. For commercial
release you need:

- v2 wire format with feature bits and a deprecation path
- S-mode + traps + paging supported inside ROI (close L3, L4, L6)
- Andes vendor CSR transport (close L21)
- `fcsr` fix (close L20)
- A proper error policy instead of `cmderr` swallowing
- A value-level handoff checker (close L15) wired into CI

Rough effort: 6-9 months of focused hardening, not weeks.

content.text:
Read all the planning docs. Here's the landscape and my proposed architecture before I write anything.

## What already exists (don't duplicate)

The engineering half of "all features" is **already broken down three times**:
- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6, closing limitations L1-L21
- `docs/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8 (same work, failure-mode view)
- `docs/limitation.md` - L1-L21 plain-English + 4/10 scorecard

And two feature roadmaps are **100% done**: the gem5-parity core (CSR/PC/icount/SimPoint + warmup) and `driver_ROADMAP.md` (hsim CLI F1-F14).

## How the ~50 FRs actually break down today

| Bucket | Count | State |
|---|---|---|
| Core engine + driver | ~13 FRs | **done/partial** (FR-101..108 M-mode, FR-114 checkpoint, FR-301 most hsim subcmds) |

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing limitations L1-L21
- `docs/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/limitation.md`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

## Track and wave ordering (dependency DAG)

```
Track E (engineering)            Track P (productization)        Track B
-----------------------          ------------------------        --------
Wave 0  loud-failure  --+        P-a interfaces (independent)    process /
        (E01..E04)      |        P-b trace export (needs E18)    legal,
           |            |        P-c observability               run in
           v            |        P-d ENCRYPTION  *ship gate*     parallel,
Wave 1  wire v2 (E05) --+----->  P-e licensing (needs P-d)       no code
           |                     P-f packaging (needs all)       dep
     +-----+-----+
     v           v
Wave 2 envelope  Wave 3 Andes
(E06..E11)       parity (E12,E13)
     |           |
     +-----+-----+
           v
Wave 4 scale (E14..E17)
           |
           v
Wave 5 accuracy + robustness (E18..E23)
           |
           v
Wave 6 portability (deferred, see Out of scope)
```

Hard dependencies:

- **F-ENG-05 (wire format v2)** gates Waves 2-4: every new state block
  (trap, S-mode, Andes, per-hart) needs feature-bitted fields.
- **F-PROD-12 (encryption)** is the commercial ship gate (MR-D). Nothing
  goes to a paying customer without it. It is also the longest pole
  (24-48 weeks, possibly an external partner - see MRD open questions).
- **P-e licensing** assumes the encrypted binary exists (P-d) to bind to.
- **P-f packaging** closes last; it bundles every shipped component.

Tracks E, P, and B run in parallel across sessions. Within Track E the
waves are sequential after Wave 1.

---

## Baseline: already shipped

These FRs are closed by the gem5-parity core roadmap (CSR / PC / icount /
SimPoint switching + warmup window) and `docs/archive/driver_ROADMAP.md`
(the `./hsim` driver F1-F14). They are the starting line, not open work.

- FR-101 three-phase handoff (`./hsim run`, M-mode envelope).
- FR-102/103/104/105 all four trigger modes.
- FR-106/107 state transport + handback for the M-mode subset: 32 GPRs,
  32 FPRs, V-state, and 4 restored CSRs (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret).
- FR-108 M-mode workloads (asm + C-runtime fixtures).
- FR-114 checkpoint / replay (`./hsim archive` + `./hsim replay`).
- FR-205 iterative re-measure (replay a checkpoint against a rebuilt vsim).
- FR-301 (partial) subcommands present: list, build, run, test, doctor,
  profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate.

"partial" elsewhere means the M-mode happy path works but the full FR
acceptance (S/U-mode, full CSR set, JSON, RTL-correlated accuracy) is open.

---

# Track E - Engineering

## Wave 0 - Truth in advertising

Goal: stop silent wrongness before fixing big things. Highest ROI per
week. (Absorbs commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 0; L11/L15/L16/L20.)

### F-ENG-01 - Value-level handoff checker

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-K(601), MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L15 (F-T3.1)
- Description: The icount and simpoint paths assert only exit code and PC
  range; a wrong register value passes silently. Add a post-handback
  `g`-packet read in the orchestrator and compare it field-by-field
  against the drained `hybrid_state_v1`. Wire it as a CI gate.
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (post-handback readback),
  `tests/hsim/test_handoff_value_check.sh` (new)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a fixture mutates a GPR mid-ROI; the checker fails when the
  drained struct disagrees with the QEMU2 post-handback readback. Today
  nothing compares them.

### F-ENG-02 - Fail-loud on missing CSR name

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-305 (exit 4), MR-K
- L-id: L16
- Description: GPR/PC writes hard-fail when the stub omits the name, but
  every CSR/PMP/V write goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns
  quietly on a missing feature-XML name. The asymmetry is the hazard.
  Make a missing CSR name raise the same way a missing GPR does, mapped
  to exit code 4 (state-transport corruption).
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:251-258` (`_try_write_u64`
  returns status), `apply_state` (caller asserts)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a mock stub that drops `mtvec`; the orchestrator must raise,
  not skip.

### F-ENG-03 - VLEN runtime check

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L11 (F-T3.4)
- Description: No runtime check that QEMU `vlenb` equals vsim `vlenb`. A
  mismatch leaves the upper bytes of each V register as scratch. Read the
  live `vlenb` at handoff and abort with a clear error on mismatch. Also
  collapse the duplicated `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES=64` constant
  (`checkpoint.py:44`) so it cannot drift from `spawn.py`.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (read live
  vlenb), `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (compare),
  `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:44`
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a VLEN=256 fixture against a VLEN=512 sim aborts at the handoff
  boundary instead of silently corrupting the V regfile.

### F-ENG-04 - fcsr / frm / fflags round-trip

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-202, MR-A
- L-id: L20 (F-T1.2)
- Description: `fcsr` (packs `frm[7:5]` + `fflags[4:0]`) is in no
  transport surface. FP work inside the ROI uses reset rounding (RNE) and
  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong. Add `uint64_t fcsr`, drain
  alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is enabled, drain before
  handback, ship via P-packet.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (field from `reserved[]`),
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (handle + drain),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (drain),
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (handback)
- Dependencies: none (additive in v1; folds into F-ENG-05's base block)
- TDD RED: `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fp_rounding.c` sets `frm=RDN`, does an FP
  op inside the ROI, asserts the result matches RDN not RNE.

## Wave 1 - Wire format v2

Goal: structural foundation. v1 has ~216 reserved bytes and no growth
path; every Wave 2-3 fix needs feature-bitted fields. (Absorbs
commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 1.)

### F-ENG-05 - hybrid_state_v2 with feature bits

- Status: not-started
- Type: structural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-801 (ABI versioning), MR-A, MR-E, MR-I
- L-id: structural foundation (limitation.md "transport ceiling")
- Description: New `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h`. Magic + version + size
  header; reader rejects unknown version. Feature bits extend the three
  existing (`RV64/FP/V`) with `PRIV`, `TRAP_CSR`, `S_MODE_CSR`,
  `ANDES_CSR`. Base block: GPRs, FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs, PC, priv. Trap
  block: mepc, mcause, mtval, dpc. S-mode block (behind bit): stvec, sepc,
  scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip, scounteren, senvcfg, satp. V block
  unchanged. Keep a v1 reader (zero-extend) for one release; drop the v1
  writer after one release. Update all 4 transports (plugin drain, vsim
  resume, vsim drain, orchestrator parse). Mirror in `abi.py`.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (new),
  `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`, `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`,
  `tools/orchestrator/abi.py`, `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`,
  `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`, `docs/wire_format_v2.md` (new)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-04 (fcsr lands in the v2 base block)
- TDD RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts the v2 magic/version header and a
  feature-bit gate (e.g. S-mode block absent when `S_MODE_CSR` clear); a
  v1 blob still reads via the shim. An ABI-hash check fails CI on an

## Wave 2 - ROI envelope expansion

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/limitation.md`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

---

## FR -> feature -> status coverage matrix

---

## Track and wave ordering (dependency DAG)

```
Track E (engineering)            Track P (productization)        Track B
-----------------------          ------------------------        --------
Wave 0  loud-failure  --+        P-a interfaces (independent)    process /
        (E01..E04)      |        P-b trace export (needs E18)    legal,
           |            |        P-c observability               run in
           v            |        P-d ENCRYPTION  *ship gate*     parallel,
Wave 1  wire v2 (E05) --+----->  P-e licensing (needs P-d)       no code
           |                     P-f packaging (needs all)       dep
     +-----+-----+
     v           v
Wave 2 envelope  Wave 3 Andes
(E06..E11)       parity (E12,E13)
     |           |
     +-----+-----+
           v
Wave 4 scale (E14..E17)
           |
           v
Wave 5 accuracy + robustness (E18..E23)
           |
           v
Wave 6 portability (deferred, see Out of scope)
```

Hard dependencies:

- **F-ENG-05 (wire format v2)** gates Waves 2-4: every new state block
  (trap, S-mode, Andes, per-hart) needs feature-bitted fields.
- **F-PROD-12 (encryption)** is the commercial ship gate (MR-D). Nothing
  goes to a paying customer without it. It is also the longest pole
  (24-48 weeks, possibly an external partner - see MRD open questions).
- **P-e licensing** assumes the encrypted binary exists (P-d) to bind to.
- **P-f packaging** closes last; it bundles every shipped component.

Tracks E, P, and B run in parallel across sessions. Within Track E the
waves are sequential after Wave 1.

---

## Baseline: already shipped

These FRs are closed by the gem5-parity core roadmap (CSR / PC / icount /
SimPoint switching + warmup window) and `docs/archive/driver_ROADMAP.md`
(the `./hsim` driver F1-F14). They are the starting line, not open work.

- FR-101 three-phase handoff (`./hsim run`, M-mode envelope).
- FR-102/103/104/105 all four trigger modes.
- FR-106/107 state transport + handback for the M-mode subset: 32 GPRs,
  32 FPRs, V-state, and 4 restored CSRs (mstatus, mtvec, mcycle, minstret).
- FR-108 M-mode workloads (asm + C-runtime fixtures).
- FR-114 checkpoint / replay (`./hsim archive` + `./hsim replay`).
- FR-205 iterative re-measure (replay a checkpoint against a rebuilt vsim).
- FR-301 (partial) subcommands present: list, build, run, test, doctor,
  profile, cluster, archive, replay, estimate.

"partial" elsewhere means the M-mode happy path works but the full FR
acceptance (S/U-mode, full CSR set, JSON, RTL-correlated accuracy) is open.

---

# Track E - Engineering

## Wave 0 - Truth in advertising

Goal: stop silent wrongness before fixing big things. Highest ROI per
week. (Absorbs commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 0; L11/L15/L16/L20.)

### F-ENG-01 - Value-level handoff checker

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-K(601), MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L15 (F-T3.1)
- Description: The icount and simpoint paths assert only exit code and PC
  range; a wrong register value passes silently. Add a post-handback
  `g`-packet read in the orchestrator and compare it field-by-field
  against the drained `hybrid_state_v1`. Wire it as a CI gate.
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (post-handback readback),
  `tests/hsim/test_handoff_value_check.sh` (new)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a fixture mutates a GPR mid-ROI; the checker fails when the
  drained struct disagrees with the QEMU2 post-handback readback. Today
  nothing compares them.

### F-ENG-02 - Fail-loud on missing CSR name

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-305 (exit 4), MR-K
- L-id: L16
- Description: GPR/PC writes hard-fail when the stub omits the name, but
  every CSR/PMP/V write goes through `_try_write_u64`, which returns
  quietly on a missing feature-XML name. The asymmetry is the hazard.
  Make a missing CSR name raise the same way a missing GPR does, mapped
  to exit code 4 (state-transport corruption).
- Key files: `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py:251-258` (`_try_write_u64`
  returns status), `apply_state` (caller asserts)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a mock stub that drops `mtvec`; the orchestrator must raise,
  not skip.

### F-ENG-03 - VLEN runtime check

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, MR-A, MR-I
- L-id: L11 (F-T3.4)
- Description: No runtime check that QEMU `vlenb` equals vsim `vlenb`. A
  mismatch leaves the upper bytes of each V register as scratch. Read the
  live `vlenb` at handoff and abort with a clear error on mismatch. Also
  collapse the duplicated `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES=64` constant
  (`checkpoint.py:44`) so it cannot drift from `spawn.py`.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (read live
  vlenb), `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (compare),
  `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py:44`
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a VLEN=256 fixture against a VLEN=512 sim aborts at the handoff
  boundary instead of silently corrupting the V regfile.

### F-ENG-04 - fcsr / frm / fflags round-trip

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-202, MR-A
- L-id: L20 (F-T1.2)
- Description: `fcsr` (packs `frm[7:5]` + `fflags[4:0]`) is in no
  transport surface. FP work inside the ROI uses reset rounding (RNE) and
  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong. Add `uint64_t fcsr`, drain
  alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is enabled, drain before
  handback, ship via P-packet.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (field from `reserved[]`),
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (handle + drain),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (drain),
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (handback)
- Dependencies: none (additive in v1; folds into F-ENG-05's base block)
- TDD RED: `tests/fixtures/rt_c_fp_rounding.c` sets `frm=RDN`, does an FP
  op inside the ROI, asserts the result matches RDN not RNE.

## Wave 1 - Wire format v2

Goal: structural foundation. v1 has ~216 reserved bytes and no growth
path; every Wave 2-3 fix needs feature-bitted fields. (Absorbs
commercial_v1_roadmap Wave 1.)

### F-ENG-05 - hybrid_state_v2 with feature bits

- Status: not-started
- Type: structural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-801 (ABI versioning), MR-A, MR-E, MR-I
- L-id: structural foundation (limitation.md "transport ceiling")
- Description: New `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h`. Magic + version + size
  header; reader rejects unknown version. Feature bits extend the three
  existing (`RV64/FP/V`) with `PRIV`, `TRAP_CSR`, `S_MODE_CSR`,
  `ANDES_CSR`. Base block: GPRs, FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs, PC, priv. Trap
  block: mepc, mcause, mtval, dpc. S-mode block (behind bit): stvec, sepc,
  scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip, scounteren, senvcfg, satp. V block
  unchanged. Keep a v1 reader (zero-extend) for one release; drop the v1
  writer after one release. Update all 4 transports (plugin drain, vsim
  resume, vsim drain, orchestrator parse). Mirror in `abi.py`.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (new),
  `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`, `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`,
  `tools/orchestrator/abi.py`, `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`,
  `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp`, `docs/wire_format_v2.md` (new)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-04 (fcsr lands in the v2 base block)
- TDD RED: `state_abi.test.cpp` asserts the v2 magic/version header and a
  feature-bit gate (e.g. S-mode block absent when `S_MODE_CSR` clear); a
  v1 blob still reads via the shim. An ABI-hash check fails CI on an
  unreviewed layout change.

## Wave 2 - ROI envelope expansion

Goal: real OS-bearing workloads run inside vsim. Removes the "M-mode only,
trap-free, PMP-static, no syscalls" core rule. (Absorbs commercial_v1
Wave 2; L1-L6.)

### F-ENG-06 - Paging (satp) restore + TLB flush

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L3
- Description: `satp` is drained but never written into vsim, so the ROI
  runs bare-mode and every virtual address hits wrong memory. Restore
  `satp` on resume, then `sfence.vma` via the Program Buffer to flush
  stale TLB.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with `satp != 0` runs a Sv39-mapped load inside the
  ROI and reads the correct mapped value.

### F-ENG-07 - Trap / exception state round-trip

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L4 (F-T1.4)
- Description: `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are not re-read at drain (stale
  QEMU1 values pass through) and trap-delegation CSRs are not restored, so
  a trap inside the ROI starts from reset. Restore the trap block on
  entry; re-read it at drain.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (re-read
  mcause/mtval/mepc), `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (restore)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture that triggers an illegal-instruction trap inside the
  ROI; the trap handler runs to completion under vsim.

### F-ENG-08 - Privilege restore (S/U-mode)

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L6 (F-T2.1)
- Description: Both sides hardcode `priv=3`. vsim never writes `dcsr.prv`
  (so `dret` always resumes M-mode); `apply_state` never writes `priv`.
  Stop hardcoding; write `dcsr.prv` so `dret` resumes in the drained mode;
  add `priv` to the handback.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp:51`,
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:264`,
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (dcsr.prv),
  `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` (apply_state priv)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture that triggers from S-mode and resumes to S-mode.

### F-ENG-09 - PMP restore into vsim

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, FR-109, MR-A
- L-id: L2 (F-T1.3)
- Description: All 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr` are drained but none are
  written into vsim, so the ROI runs with zeroed PMP and any protection
  silently disappears. Write all PMP via abstract command; respect
  locked-bit semantics.
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with a write-protect PMP region; a write inside the
  ROI traps.

### F-ENG-10 - LR/SC reservation policy

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-106, MR-A
- L-id: L5 (F-T1.5)
- Description: A reservation held across the trigger never round-trips, so
  the `sc` always fails and a CAS loop spins forever. v1.0: the plugin
  REJECTS the handoff with a clear error if a reservation is pending at
  the trigger (no silent miscompare). Carrying the reservation in the wire
  format is deferred post-v1.
- Key files: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (reservation check),
  `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (reservation field behind a feature bit,
  post-v1)
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: a fixture with `lr` before and `sc` after the trigger; the
  plugin aborts at the trigger with a clear message, not a spin.

### F-ENG-11 - Syscalls / semihosting inside ROI

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-109, MR-B
- L-id: L1 (F-T1.1) - the blocker
- Description: libgloss inside the ROI emits the semihosting magic triple;
  vsim has no handler, so the ebreak trap-loops to timeout. Policy
  (decide before implementation): (a) passthrough - vsim catches the
  semihosting ebreak and proxies to a host syscall trampoline (heavy,
  accurate; recommended for commercial v1); (b) detect+warn+skip (cheap,
  lossy; v0.x interim).
- Key files: `verilator/src/hybrid/semihosting.hpp` (new), platform trap
  handler hook; `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05, F-ENG-07 (trap plumbing)
- TDD RED: a `printf` inside the ROI completes (policy a) or logs one
  skip warning (policy b) instead of timing out.

## Wave 3 - Andes parity

Goal: vendor-specific CSRs round-trip; the trigger stops colliding with a
real CSR. (Absorbs commercial_v1 Wave 3; L12/L21.)

### F-ENG-12 - Andes vendor CSR transport

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-401, FR-106, MR-E
- L-id: L21
- Description: Zero Andes CSRs are transported today. Cache/prefetcher/BP
  controls shape the cycle figure, so this is an accuracy hazard, not only
  correctness. Add an ANDES_CSR block (v2). Label each CSR
  software-visible (restore into vsim) or microarch-only (drain + handback
  only): `mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg` are software-visible;
  `mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg` are microarch.
  Ensure the QEMU fork feature XML advertises all of them.
- Key files: `include/hybrid/state_abi_v2.h` (ANDES_CSR block),
  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (Andes handles),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (software-visible restore),
  QEMU fork feature XML
- Dependencies: F-ENG-05
- TDD RED: toggling an Andes cache-enable CSR before the ROI changes the
  measured cycle figure; the CSR round-trips bit-exactly to QEMU2.

### F-ENG-13 - Trigger redesign off CSR 0x7C0

- Status: not-started
- Type: behavioural
- Traces: FR-102, FR-401, MR-A, MR-E
- L-id: L12
- Description: CSR `0x7C0` is a real Andes vendor CSR; the default trigger
  repurposes `csrwi 0x7C0,0/1`, so a legitimate write false-triggers.
  Move the trigger to a dedicated debug CSR (e.g. `dscratch1` with a magic
  value) or a marker instruction. Keep CSR-0x7C0 behind
  `--trigger=legacy-7c0` for one release.
- Key files: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (CSR matcher),
  `verilator/src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp`
- Dependencies: F-ENG-12 (so 0x7C0 is preserved as real state)
- TDD RED: a workload that legitimately writes `0x7C0,1` does NOT trigger
  a handoff under the new default; the new marker does.

## Wave 4 - Scale

## Out of scope (v1.0)

Deferred; documented as limits, pulled in only on customer demand.

- **Portability (commercial_v1 Wave 6)**: parameterize V-scratch GPA /
  machine / CPU model (L10), byte-swap + ABI-hash path for non-x86 hosts
  (L18), RVC CSR-marker support (L13, no action until RVC adds a CSR-write
  encoding). v1.0 ships andes_ae350 + ax45mpv + x86-64 host only.
- Non-Andes RISC-V ISA variants (FRS 1.2).
- QEMU + cycle-side Alioth (FRS 1.2; future in MRD).
- FPGA backend, cloud SaaS delivery (FRS 1.2).
- Multi-cluster cache coherence beyond a single Andes cluster (FRS 1.2).
- Vector `V` beyond AndeStar V5 (FRS 1.2).
- D23v core (FR-401 defers it to v1.1).
- LR/SC reservation carried in the wire format (F-ENG-10 phase 2, post-v1).

content.text:
Next item: **F-ENG-01 - Value-level handoff checker** (Wave 0, first thing to build).

**The problem (simple):**
When the round-trip runs in icount/simpoint mode, we only check two things at the end:
1. Did the program exit OK?
2. Did the PC (program counter) land in the right range?

We do **not** check the actual register values. So if a register holds a wrong number after the handoff, nobody notices. The test still passes. This is silent wrongness - the worst kind, because you trust a number that is lying.

**The fix (simple):**
After QEMU2 finishes, ask it for all its register values (a gdb `g`-packet read). Then compare those values one-by-one against the `hybrid_state_v1` struct we drained from vsim. If any field disagrees, fail loudly. Wire this into CI so it runs every time.

**Input -> Output:**
- Input: the drained state struct (from vsim) + QEMU2's live registers (after handback).
- Output: pass if every field matches; loud failure naming the mismatched field if not.

**Files:**
- `tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py` - add the post-handback readback + compare.
- `tests/hsim/test_handoff_value_check.sh` - new test.

**TDD RED (the failing test you write first):**
A fixture changes a GPR in the middle of the ROI. The checker must fail because the drained struct disagrees with QEMU2's readback. Today nothing compares them, so the test cannot pass until you build the checker.

**Why it is first:** no dependencies, highest value per week. It stops us shipping wrong numbers before we spend months on the big features (S-mode, paging, encryption). Truth before scale.

content.text:
MR-G is **already reachable today for M-mode workloads** - the loop exists. It is `hsim archive` + `hsim replay`. The remaining work is (1) making it work for *Linux* workloads and (2) proving the 5-minute number.

MR-G traces to 4 FRs. Status from the ROADMAP:

| FR | What it gives MR-G | Status |
|----|--------------------|--------|
| FR-101 | the handoff itself | done (M-mode) |
| FR-114 | checkpoint once, replay many | done (M-mode) |
| FR-205 | re-measure in <= 5 min | done (mechanism) |
| FR-703 | survive an engine upgrade | **not-started (F-PROD-22)** |

**The loop, in simple steps (works now):**
1. Boot the workload once in QEMU1 -> `hsim archive` saves the checkpoint.
2. Change a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth) in the vsim config.
3. Rebuild **vsim only** (`scripts/build_vsim.sh`) - do not rebuild QEMU.
4. `hsim replay` re-runs vsim against the **same** checkpoint. No re-boot.
5. Read the new cycle figure.

That is exactly the MRD picture: edit -> rebuild engine -> re-measure, no boot.

**What is still missing to fully "reach" MR-G:**

1. **Real (Linux) workloads.** FR-114's headline test is "boot Linux once (~30 min), run 10 ROIs". Booting Linux needs S-mode + paging + syscalls, which are **not** done. That is Wave 2: F-ENG-05 (wire v2) -> F-ENG-06 (paging), F-ENG-08 (S/U-mode), F-ENG-11 (syscalls). Until then the loop only runs bare-metal M-mode fixtures.

2. **Proof of <= 5 min.** FR-205 says the mechanism is done, but the acceptance ("3 microarch tweaks measured <= 5 min") is not proven by a harness. The cleanest place to add this is alongside **F-ENG-23** (the wall-clock timing harness) - add an edit-rebuild-replay timing case.

3. **Durability across engine versions (F-PROD-22).** Today replay assumes the same engine build. When you ship an N+1 engine, old checkpoints must still replay or fail with a clear message. That needs **F-ENG-05** (checkpoint format versioning) + **F-PROD-20** (installer), then **F-PROD-22** (upgrade-in-place).

**Shortest path to claim MR-G:**

```
NOW (M-mode loop) ----------------------> usable today
   +  F-ENG-23 timing case  ------------> proves <= 5 min  (FR-205 acceptance)
   +  Wave 2 (E05->E06/E08/E11) --------> Linux workloads  (FR-114 real acceptance)
   +  E05 + F-PROD-20 -> F-PROD-22 -----> upgrade-safe     (FR-703)
```

So: the **flywheel already spins** for M-mode. To turn it into the commercial MR-G, the gating dependency is **F-ENG-05 (wire format v2)** - it unlocks the Linux envelope (Wave 2) and the versioned checkpoints (F-PROD-22). The 5-minute proof is cheap and independent. None of this is new architecture; it is finishing the envelope the loop runs inside.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Convert config.yaml to a CMake-includeable file with set() calls."""

import sys
import yaml


def main():
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print(f"Usage: {sys.argv[0]} <config.yaml> <output.cmake>", file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)

    config_path = sys.argv[1]
    output_path = sys.argv[2]

    with open(config_path, "r") as f:
        data = yaml.safe_load(f)

    cpus = data.get("cpus", {})
    lines = []
    lines.append("# Auto-generated from config.yaml — do not edit")
    lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_LIST {" ".join(cpus.keys())})')
    lines.append("")

    for name, cfg in cpus.items():
        upper = name.upper()
        lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_SERIES "{cfg["cpu_series"]}")')
        lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_RTL_PACKAGE "{cfg["rtl_package"]}")')
        lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_CPP_WRAPPER "{cfg["cpp_wrapper"]}")')
        lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_CONFIG "{cfg["config"]}")')
        lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_CONFIG_DIR "{cfg["config_dir"]}")')
        lines.append(
            f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_CONFIG_INC_FILTER "{cfg.get("config_inc_filter", "")}")'
        )
        lines.append(
            f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_EXTRA_VERILATOR_FLAGS "{cfg.get("extra_verilator_flags", "")}")'
        )
        ace_path = cfg.get("libaceasim_path") or ""
        lines.append(f'set(VSIM_CPU_{upper}_LIBACEASIM_PATH "{ace_path}")')
        lines.append("")

    with open(output_path, "w") as f:
        f.write("\n".join(lines))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

content.text:
Verified end to end. Here is the honest answer.

## Short answer

**"ROB depth" is not a knob** - the ax45mpv is an in-order core, there is no reorder buffer. The real cycle-engine knobs live as `` `define NDS_* `` macros in **one file**:

```
verilator/external/ax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl/config.inc
```

The vsim build reads **this file** (not the `.cfg`). To change a parameter: edit the define(s), rebuild vsim, replay. But **cache size is not a one-line edit** - read on.

## How the build consumes it (so you can trust the file)

```
config.yaml (rtl_package: ax45mpv_premium, config_dir: .../top/hdl)
   -> CMake copies external/ax45mpv_premium/.../config.inc into the build tree
   -> dump_verilator_defines.py --config-inc config.inc   (extracts `define lines)
   -> filter_verilog_defines.py  --filter "grep '^`define NDS_'"
   -> the NDS_* macros are fed to Verilator as the RTL config
```

The `.cfg` (`data/configs/ax45mpv_premium.cfg`) is **declared but never consumed** by the vsim build - it is the Andes IP-configurator's record. Do not edit it expecting an effect. `config.inc` is git-tracked (inside the `external/ax45mpv_premium` submodule), so your edit is the real input and the build will not overwrite it.

## Two classes of knob

**Class 1 - clean single-define (safe to change one line):**

| Define | Now | What it does |
|--------|-----|--------------|
| `NDS_BRANCH_PREDICTION` | `"btb256"` | branch predictor |
| `NDS_DCACHE_PREFETCH_SUPPORT` | `"no"` | D-cache prefetcher on/off |
| `NDS_MSHR_DEPTH` | `3` | outstanding D-cache misses |
| `NDS_LSU_SB_DEPTH` | `0` | store buffer depth |
| `NDS_VLSU_MSHR_DEPTH` | `16` | vector LSU MSHRs |

**Class 2 - cache size/way (NOT one line):** size, ways, and the RAM-array dimensions are separate defines that must stay consistent:

```
NDS_DCACHE_SIZE_KB   32     <- 32 KB
NDS_DCACHE_WAY        4      <- 4-way, 64B line  => 128 sets
NDS_DCACHE_TAG_RAM_AW   7    <- log2(128 sets)         (must match)
NDS_DCACHE_DATA_RAM_AW  10   <- 1024 x 64b per way = 8KB*4 = 32KB (must match)
```

If you bump `SIZE_KB` to 64 but leave the RAM `AW` values, you get an inconsistent model (wrong behaviour or a verilate error). The Andes configurator normally recomputes these together - **that generator is not in this repo** (only synthesis/FPGA TCL), so by hand you must update the whole coupled set. And nothing here validates consistency - it ties directly to the Wave 0 "fail loud" gap.

## The procedure

```sh
# 1. edit the define(s) in the submodule
$EDITOR verilator/external/ax45mpv_premium/andes_ip/kv_core/top/hdl/config.inc
# 2. rebuild vsim only (re-verilates the core)
./scripts/build_vsim.sh
# 3. re-measure against the existing checkpoint, no re-boot
./hsim replay <checkpoint>
```

## The MR-G catch you should know as PM

MR-G's acceptance is "edit-rebuild-measure **under 5 minutes**." A `config.inc` change **re-verilates the whole core** (Verilator + g++ on the full Andes RTL), which is typically tens of minutes, not 5. So:

- The **< 5 min loop is real** for re-measuring the *same* engine (`hsim replay` against a checkpoint) - e.g. after an orchestrator or non-RTL change.
- For an actual **RTL-parameter change** (cache, predictor), the bottleneck is re-verilation, not boot. "Rebuild engine only" saves the 30-min QEMU boot, but you still pay the verilate cost.

Worth deciding with the team whether MR-G's 5-min target means "re-measure" (achievable now) or "re-parameterize the RTL" (needs incremental-verilate work, currently out of scope).

```
`define NDS_DCACHE_PREFETCH_SUPPORT "no"     ->  "yes"     # prefetcher on
`define NDS_MSHR_DEPTH              3         ->  8         # more outstanding misses
`define NDS_BRANCH_PREDICTION       "btb256"  ->  ...       # predictor
`define NDS_LSU_SB_DEPTH            0         ->  4         # store buffer
```
Flip one value, rebuild, replay. Done.

**Cache size in KB is the hard one - NOT 1 line.** Four lines must agree:
```
`define NDS_DCACHE_SIZE_KB     32   # the size
`define NDS_DCACHE_WAY         4    # ways
`define NDS_DCACHE_TAG_RAM_AW  7    # set-index bits  (depends on size+way)
`define NDS_DCACHE_DATA_RAM_AW 10   # data-array bits (depends on size+way)
```
If you change only `SIZE_KB`, the RAM arrays stay the old size and the model is wrong. The Andes config tool normally fixes all four together, but **that tool is not in this repo**, so by hand you must recompute the two `RAM_AW` lines. I can compute them for a target size if you tell me the number.

**ROB depth:** this core is in-order. There is no ROB. That knob does not exist.

Want me to actually do one now? I can flip `NDS_DCACHE_PREFETCH_SUPPORT` to `"yes"`, rebuild vsim (tens of minutes - it re-verilates the core), and show you the cycle number change. Say go.

input.description: Check if built RTL core is single or multi-hart

content.text:
Multi-hart = run more than 1 hart (hardware thread) through the same QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 round-trip, each hart carrying its own register state. Today every path is hard-wired to hart 0. The roadmap already tracks this as **F-ENG-14** (transport) and **F-ENG-15** (coherence).

## Blocker first (Step 0): the engine you build now is a 1-hart core
`config.inc:56` sets `` `define NDS_NHART 1 ``. With one hart in the RTL there is no second hart to halt, restore into, or measure. So **before any software work**, rebuild vsim from a config with `NDS_NHART 2` (or 4/8). No second hart in RTL = nothing to transport into.

## Core shape - 3 things change, in this order

**1. The wire format must hold N harts.** (needs F-ENG-05, the v2 format first)
`hybrid_state_v1` describes ONE hart: a single `hart_id` plus one set of `gpr[]/fpr[]/csr/vreg[]` (`state_abi.h:44-89`). v2 = an array of these, one entry per hart.

**2. The Debug Module must select each hart by `hartsel`. This is the key missing piece.**
I checked every `dmcontrol` write - `resume_driver.hpp:69,150,155` and `state_drain.hpp:42-43` only ever set `dmactive`/`haltreq`/`resumereq`. The hart-select field is **never set**, so it always means hart 0. To restore hart 1 you must write `hartsel` into `dmcontrol` first, then run the same abstract-command / program-buffer sequence. New shape: `for each hart: set hartsel -> halt -> restore that hart's state`. Same loop for drain.

**3. Trigger and counter must be per-hart.**
- icount is one `uint64_t` counter (`icount_trigger.hpp:14,47`) -> one per hart.
- BBV emit is single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`).
- The QEMU plugin already knows the vcpu (`hybrid_handoff.c:263` sets `s.hart_id = vcpu_idx`) but drains one vcpu to one file -> drain all vcpus.

**Then remove the guard:** `runner.py:212-213` rejects `hart_id != 0`. Delete it once the path works.

## TDD RED test (per F-ENG-14)
A 2-hart fixture where hart 0 and hart 1 start with **different** register values; after the round-trip each hart must resume from its OWN state. Write this first - it fails today on both the guard and the single-hart transport.

## Two features, not one
- **F-ENG-14** = the transport above. Enough if harts run independently (no shared coherent data in the measured region).
- **F-ENG-15** = ACE coherence (directory + snoop filter). Needed ONLY if the harts share memory and the cycle count depends on hardware cache coherence. Much harder, depends on F-ENG-14.

Which path you need depends on your target workload - that decides the scope, so:

questions.question: In the measured region, do the harts share memory through hardware cache coherence (e.g. threads hitting the same cache lines), or do they run independently?

options.label: Independent harts
options.description: Each hart works on its own data; no shared coherent cache lines in the ROI. Scope = F-ENG-14 transport only. Recommended as the first bring-up step.

options.label: Coherent shared memory
options.description: Threads share data and the cycle count depends on cache coherence (MESI/snoop traffic). Adds F-ENG-15 ACE transport (directory + snoop filter) - a much larger effort on top of F-ENG-14.

questions.question: How many harts should the cycle engine (RTL) be built for? This sets the NDS_NHART rebuild in Step 0.

options.description: Matches the roadmap RED test (2-hart round-trip). Smallest real multi-hart proof; fastest to verilate.
Common small-cluster config; larger build and longer verilate time.
Larger cluster; longest verilate time and most simulation overhead per run.

content.text:
Yes - much harder. Today's "userspace" ROI is **bare-metal**: it runs in M-mode (highest privilege), no OS, no virtual memory, no traps, no syscalls. The handoff just copies registers + physical RAM and runs. Linux breaks every one of those assumptions. That is why MR-B maps to **five** not-started features (F-ENG-06,07,08,11,17 via FR-109, `ROADMAP.md:52`), while bare-metal userspace already works.

Four jumps from bare-metal to Linux:

**1. Privilege stack (U + S + M).**
Bare-metal is M-mode only - `priv` is hardcoded to `3` in both `hybrid_handoff.c:264` and `state_drain.hpp:51`. Linux runs the hot loop in U-mode (priv 0) on an S-mode kernel on M-mode firmware. You must capture the real priv level and the S-mode CSRs - and the ABI has **none** today (only M-mode CSRs + satp, `state_abi.h:55-67`). F-ENG-05 adds the S-mode block (sstatus/sepc/scause/stval/stvec/sscratch/sie/sip); F-ENG-08 restores it.

**2. Virtual memory (MMU). The biggest structural blocker.**
Bare-metal uses physical addresses; the shared mmap is physical. The built engine has **no MMU**: `config.inc:159` sets `NDS_MMU_SCHEME "bare"`, STLB entries 0. Linux uses Sv39 paging - the hot loop's addresses are virtual and `satp` points to page tables in RAM. Two parts: (a) rebuild vsim with an MMU config (`NDS_MMU_SCHEME "sv39"` + real STLB RAM dims) - the same kind of RTL rebuild as the NHART blocker; (b) restore `satp` then `sfence.vma` to flush the TLB (F-ENG-06 - today satp is drained but never written into vsim). You cannot restore satp into a core that has no MMU hardware.

**3. Traps and interrupts.**
The core rule is "vsim phase is trap-free" (CLAUDE.md). Linux is never trap-free: the timer interrupt ticks, first-touch pages fault. The trap CSRs pass through unrestored today, so a trap in the ROI starts from reset. F-ENG-07 restores the trap block and lets vsim take traps.

**4. Syscalls.**
Linux userspace does `ecall` into the kernel. Today's rule is "no syscalls in the ROI" - vsim has no handler, so the trap loops to timeout. Need a trap/syscall policy (F-ENG-11).

Practical cost on top: Linux boots in ~30 min, so you need a post-boot checkpoint to iterate (FR-114 - the `hsim archive`/`replay` loop already exists for M-mode); bigger RAM (F-ENG-16); device/MMIO access inside the ROI (F-ENG-17).

**One-line summary:** bare-metal userspace = "copy registers + physical RAM, run, copy back." Linux = "also reproduce the full privilege stack, page tables, live traps, and the syscall boundary - on an engine currently built with no MMU and assuming no traps." All of it sits behind the v2 wire format (F-ENG-05).

1	# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document
2	
3	Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
4	Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.
5	
6	Companion docs:
7	- `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)
8	- `ROADMAP.md` - master feature roadmap (engineering plan; supersedes
9	  `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md`)
10	- `docs/limitation.md` - current ROI envelope (alpha)
11	
12	This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
13	external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
14	Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
15	commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
16	Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Executive Summary
21	
22	**Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
23	**Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
24	**Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)
25	**Fast engine**: QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin
26	**Target customer**: Andes IP licensees doing pre-silicon perf work
27	**Tier / price band**: Tier 2, $K-M/year per-seat or per-project
28	**Ship target**: Commercial v1.0 in ~12 months (engineering) +
29	6-12 months (encryption tooling) = ~18-24 months from today
30	**Differentiation**: only Tier-2 hybrid product with first-class
31	Andes IP (vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5 extensions) and zero FPGA
32	capex requirement
33	
34	**The one-line pitch**: "Cycle-exact RISC-V perf measurement on
35	real customer workloads, without an FPGA emulator or a multi-year
36	RTL learning curve."
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Product Definition
41	
42	What the customer buys:
43	
44	| Component | Delivery | Purpose |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `hsim` driver CLI | binary | orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff |
47	| QEMU (Andes fork) | binary + plugin SO | fast-forward engine, runs boring 99% |
48	| vsim cycle engine | **encrypted** binary | cycle-exact ROI measurement, RTL-derived but not RTL-recoverable |
49	| State transport library | linked into both | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format, mmap RAM |
50	| Trigger toolkit | linked + headers | magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint |
51	| Pipeline trace converter | binary | kanata / Clarity DB output |
52	| Reference flow | scripts + sample workloads | bare-metal kernel, Linux userspace, SPEC-class harness |
53	| License daemon | binary | per-seat / per-project enforcement |
54	| Documentation | PDF + HTML | user guide, ABI reference, integration guide |
55	| Support | contracted | tiered SLA |
56	
57	What the customer does NOT get:
58	- Raw Verilator C++ output (encrypted only)
59	- Andes RTL or microarch internals
60	- Source of the cycle engine
61	- QEMU source (binary only; upstream QEMU available separately)
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 3. Target Market & Buyer Personas
66	
67	### 3.1 Primary buyer: Andes IP licensee SoC integrator
68	
69	| Attribute | Profile |
70	|---|---|
71	| Company size | 50-2000 engineers; cannot justify $M+ ZeBu capex |
72	| Andes IP | one or more of AX25 / AX27 / AX45 / AX46 / D23v |
73	| Workload class | OS + userspace apps, AI inference kernels, networking dataplane |
74	| Pain | QEMU is too coarse; FPGA is too late; Alioth alone is too slow on real workloads |
75	| Buying authority | Engineering VP + IT procurement; budget cycle 6-12 months |
76	| Price tolerance | $20K-200K/seat/year, $200K-2M project license |
77	
78	### 3.2 Secondary buyer: research lab / university with industry tie-in
79	
80	| Attribute | Profile |
81	|---|---|
82	| Use case | Microarchitecture research, comparative perf studies |
83	| Procurement | Grant-funded; multi-year |
84	| Price tolerance | Academic discount tier; $5K-20K/seat/year |
85	| Value to Andes | Reference publications, conference visibility, talent pipeline |
86	
87	### 3.3 Personas at the buying customer
88	
89	| Role | What they care about |
90	|---|---|
91	| **SoC Architect** | accuracy vs RTL, modeling fidelity of vendor CSRs |
92	| **Perf Engineer** | wall-clock turnaround, SimPoint coverage, kanata output |
93	| **DV Engineer** | reproducibility, deterministic mode, log capture |
94	| **Engineering VP / buyer** | total cost vs FPGA capex, support SLA, lifecycle |
95	| **Legal / IP officer** | encryption guarantees, no RTL leakage, license terms |
96	| **IT / DevOps** | install footprint, license server, CI integration |
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 4. Market Sizing & Opportunity
101	
102	Rough TAM estimate (top-down):
103	
104	- Andes IP active licensees: ~300 worldwide (public Andes 2025 figures)
105	- Fraction doing serious pre-silicon perf work: ~30% = ~90 accounts
106	- Fraction with ROI-style workloads (OS + hot kernel): ~60% = ~54 accounts
107	- Realistic 3-year capture rate: 20% = ~11 paying accounts
108	- Average deal size: $100K-500K/year
109	- Year-3 ARR target: $1.1M-5.5M
110	
111	Adjacent expansion:
112	- Non-Andes RISC-V vendors (SiFive, MIPS, Tenstorrent) could license
113	  the QEMU plugin + state transport without Andes-specific vendor
114	  CSRs. Out of scope for v1.0 but TAM-meaningful.
115	- Internal Andes engineering teams (~200 engineers) consume the
116	  product at internal cost; counts as cost avoidance vs ZeBu rental.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 5. Competitive Positioning
121	
122	### 5.1 Competitive matrix (commercial Tier 2 focus)
123	
124	| Product | Vendor | Strength | Weakness vs HybridSim | Price band |
125	|---|---|---|---|---|
126	| ARM Cycle Models + Fast Models | ARM | mature, encrypted, CADI ecosystem | ARM-only ISA; no Andes IP; per-core not full cluster | $100K-1M/yr |
127	| Imperas (now Synopsys) | Synopsys | RISC-V leader; DPI-to-RTL | functional ISS + RTL bridge, not true hybrid; expensive | $200K-2M/yr |
128	| Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Wind River | full-system; large install base | not cycle-exact; weak RISC-V perf modeling | $50K-500K/yr |
129	| **Andes HybridSim** | **Andes** | **first-class Andes IP, $0 cycle-side capex, bundled SimPoint/kanata** | **alpha today; Andes ISA only** | **$K-M/yr** |
130	
131	Tier 1 (ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce) is explicitly not our competitive
132	target. They serve customers who already have $M+ FPGA capex.
133	
134	Tier 3 (gem5, Spike+DPI) is not our competitive target either.
135	Open-source pulls revenue to zero; we ship Andes IP correlation as
136	a paid product.
137	
138	### 5.2 The wedge
139	
140	Three things competitors do not deliver together:
141	
142	1. **First-class Andes IP modeling** - vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5,
143	   Andes platform (AE350-class) out of the box. ARM and Imperas

145	2. **Zero FPGA capex** - runs on a Linux workstation. ZeBu/Palladium

147	3. **Bundled SimPoint + kanata + handoff orchestrator** - competitors

149

151	
152	- vsim cycle-side speed (5-50 KHz) is 1000-10000x slower than ZeBu
153	  emulator (10-100 MHz). For ROIs longer than ~1B cycles, ZeBu wins.
154	  Mitigation: SimPoint clustering shrinks effective ROI.
155	- ISA coverage is RISC-V Andes-only. ARM Cycle Models cover ARM
156	  ecosystem; Imperas covers broad RISC-V. Mitigation: deepen Andes
157	  IP support to make depth beat breadth.
158	- Maturity: ARM Cycle Models are 10+ years productized. Our v1.0

164	## 6. Business Model
165	
166	### 6.1 Pricing structure
167	
168	Three SKUs:
169	
170	| SKU | Audience | Includes | Price guidance |
171	|---|---|---|---|

176	Add-ons (post-v1.0):
177	- Linux/SMP support pack (multi-hart, S/U-mode beyond v1.0 envelope)
178	- Custom Andes IP variant support (one-off NRE)
179	- Premium SLA (24h response, dedicated FAE)
180	
181	### 6.2 License enforcement
182	
183	- Network license daemon (FlexLM-class) per industry norm
184	- Node-locked option for air-gapped customers (HSM-bound)
185	- Floating pool with checkout / checkin
186	- Per-feature flags (kanata, SimPoint, vendor CSR pack)

188	
189	### 6.3 Delivery channels
190	
191	- Direct (Andes sales) for top-50 accounts
192	- Distributor / reseller for long tail (e.g. through Andes regional

196	---

198	## 7. Market Requirements
199	
200	Numbered MRs for traceability into FRS.md. Each MR has a status
201	relative to v1.0 ship.
202	
203	### MR-A - Cycle-exact ROI measurement on customer workloads
204	
205	Customer provides their own ELF (closed source). HybridSim
206	fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
207	cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.
208	
209	- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
210	  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.
211	
212	### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI
213

215	measure, hand back to QEMU.

217	- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace

221

233	
234	- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
235	  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.
236

238	
239	All customer-visible Andes vendor CSRs and ACE coherence flows
240	round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.
241	
242	- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite passes 100%; ACE
243	  coherence regression passes on multi-hart workloads.
244	
245	### MR-F - Pipeline trace export (kanata)
246	
247	Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle
248	window with output byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline.
249	
250	- Acceptance: kanata diff against fully-RTL baseline is empty for
251	  the post-warmup window.
252

254	
255	Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
256	rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
257	checkpoint without re-running boot.
258	
259	- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a
260	  reference workload.
261	
262	### MR-H - Multi-hart support
263	
264	At least 4 harts in the cycle engine with coherent state transport
265	through ACE.
266	
267	- Acceptance: a 4-hart parallel kernel round-trips and produces a
268	  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
269	
270	### MR-I - Determinism and reproducibility
271	
272	Identical inputs (ELF + config + seed) produce bit-identical cycle
273	counts and pipeline traces across runs and hosts.
274	
275	- Acceptance: a reproducibility test suite runs the same workload
276	  on 3 different hosts; all outputs bit-identical.
277	
278	### MR-J - CI / batch integration
279	
280	The product runs unattended in a CI environment. License daemon,
281	checkpointing, error reporting, and exit codes are CI-friendly.
282	
283	- Acceptance: a reference CI pipeline (GitLab / Jenkins) runs 20
284	  workloads in parallel, collects results, no manual intervention.
285	
286	### MR-K - First-class observability
287	
288	Every handoff, trigger, and state transport event is logged with
289	structured key=value format. Errors are actionable, not "internal
290	error".
291	
292	- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a
