# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document

Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.

Companion docs:
- `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)
- `ROADMAP.md` - master feature roadmap (engineering plan; supersedes
  `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md`)
- `docs/limitation.md` - current ROI envelope (alpha)

This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.

---

## 1. Executive Summary

**Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
**Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
**Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)
**Fast engine**: QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin
**Target customer**: Andes IP licensees doing pre-silicon perf work
**Tier / price band**: Tier 2, $K-M/year per-seat or per-project
**Ship target**: Commercial v1.0 in ~12 months (engineering) +
6-12 months (encryption tooling) = ~18-24 months from today
**Differentiation**: only Tier-2 hybrid product with first-class
Andes IP (vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5 extensions) and zero FPGA
capex requirement

**The one-line pitch**: "Cycle-exact RISC-V perf measurement on
real customer workloads, without an FPGA emulator or a multi-year
RTL learning curve."

---

## 2. Product Definition

What the customer buys:

| Component | Delivery | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `hsim` driver CLI | binary | orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff |
| QEMU (Andes fork) | binary + plugin SO | fast-forward engine, runs boring 99% |
| vsim cycle engine | **encrypted** binary | cycle-exact ROI measurement, RTL-derived but not RTL-recoverable |
| State transport library | linked into both | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format, mmap RAM |
| Trigger toolkit | linked + headers | magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint |
| Pipeline trace converter | binary | kanata / Clarity DB output |
| Reference flow | scripts + sample workloads | bare-metal kernel, Linux userspace, SPEC-class harness |
| License daemon | binary | per-seat / per-project enforcement |
| Documentation | PDF + HTML | user guide, ABI reference, integration guide |
| Support | contracted | tiered SLA |

What the customer does NOT get:
- Raw Verilator C++ output (encrypted only)
- Andes RTL or microarch internals
- Source of the cycle engine
- QEMU source (binary only; upstream QEMU available separately)

---

## 3. Target Market & Buyer Personas

### 3.1 Primary buyer: Andes IP licensee SoC integrator

| Attribute | Profile |
|---|---|
| Company size | 50-2000 engineers; cannot justify $M+ ZeBu capex |
| Andes IP | one or more of AX25 / AX27 / AX45 / AX46 / D23v |
| Workload class | OS + userspace apps, AI inference kernels, networking dataplane |
| Pain | QEMU is too coarse; FPGA is too late; Alioth alone is too slow on real workloads |
| Buying authority | Engineering VP + IT procurement; budget cycle 6-12 months |
| Price tolerance | $20K-200K/seat/year, $200K-2M project license |

### 3.2 Secondary buyer: research lab / university with industry tie-in

| Attribute | Profile |
|---|---|
| Use case | Microarchitecture research, comparative perf studies |
| Procurement | Grant-funded; multi-year |
| Price tolerance | Academic discount tier; $5K-20K/seat/year |
| Value to Andes | Reference publications, conference visibility, talent pipeline |

### 3.3 Personas at the buying customer

| Role | What they care about |
|---|---|
| **SoC Architect** | accuracy vs RTL, modeling fidelity of vendor CSRs |
| **Perf Engineer** | wall-clock turnaround, SimPoint coverage, kanata output |
| **DV Engineer** | reproducibility, deterministic mode, log capture |
| **Engineering VP / buyer** | total cost vs FPGA capex, support SLA, lifecycle |
| **Legal / IP officer** | encryption guarantees, no RTL leakage, license terms |
| **IT / DevOps** | install footprint, license server, CI integration |

---

## 4. Market Sizing & Opportunity

Rough TAM estimate (top-down):

- Andes IP active licensees: ~300 worldwide (public Andes 2025 figures)
- Fraction doing serious pre-silicon perf work: ~30% = ~90 accounts
- Fraction with ROI-style workloads (OS + hot kernel): ~60% = ~54 accounts
- Realistic 3-year capture rate: 20% = ~11 paying accounts
- Average deal size: $100K-500K/year
- Year-3 ARR target: $1.1M-5.5M

Adjacent expansion:
- Non-Andes RISC-V vendors (SiFive, MIPS, Tenstorrent) could license
  the QEMU plugin + state transport without Andes-specific vendor
  CSRs. Out of scope for v1.0 but TAM-meaningful.
- Internal Andes engineering teams (~200 engineers) consume the
  product at internal cost; counts as cost avoidance vs ZeBu rental.

---

## 5. Competitive Positioning

### 5.1 Competitive matrix (commercial Tier 2 focus)

| Product | Vendor | Strength | Weakness vs HybridSim | Price band |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ARM Cycle Models + Fast Models | ARM | mature, encrypted, CADI ecosystem | ARM-only ISA; no Andes IP; per-core not full cluster | $100K-1M/yr |
| Imperas (now Synopsys) | Synopsys | RISC-V leader; DPI-to-RTL | functional ISS + RTL bridge, not true hybrid; expensive | $200K-2M/yr |
| Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Wind River | full-system; large install base | not cycle-exact; weak RISC-V perf modeling | $50K-500K/yr |
| **Andes HybridSim** | **Andes** | **first-class Andes IP, $0 cycle-side capex, bundled SimPoint/kanata** | **alpha today; Andes ISA only** | **$K-M/yr** |

Tier 1 (ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce) is explicitly not our competitive
target. They serve customers who already have $M+ FPGA capex.

Tier 3 (gem5, Spike+DPI) is not our competitive target either.
Open-source pulls revenue to zero; we ship Andes IP correlation as
a paid product.

### 5.2 The wedge

Three things competitors do not deliver together:

1. **First-class Andes IP modeling** - vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5,
   Andes platform (AE350-class) out of the box. ARM and Imperas
   require customer integration work; Wind River is functional-only.
2. **Zero FPGA capex** - runs on a Linux workstation. ZeBu/Palladium
   need a $M+ board.
3. **Bundled SimPoint + kanata + handoff orchestrator** - competitors
   sell these as separate add-ons or do not ship them at all.

### 5.3 Honest losses

- vsim cycle-side speed (5-50 KHz) is 1000-10000x slower than ZeBu
  emulator (10-100 MHz). For ROIs longer than ~1B cycles, ZeBu wins.
  Mitigation: SimPoint clustering shrinks effective ROI.
- ISA coverage is RISC-V Andes-only. ARM Cycle Models cover ARM
  ecosystem; Imperas covers broad RISC-V. Mitigation: deepen Andes
  IP support to make depth beat breadth.
- Maturity: ARM Cycle Models are 10+ years productized. Our v1.0
  is a fresh product. Mitigation: design-partner program before
  general availability.

---

## 6. Business Model

### 6.1 Pricing structure

Three SKUs:

| SKU | Audience | Includes | Price guidance |
|---|---|---|---|
| **HybridSim Workstation** | per-seat developer | full feature set, 1 named seat | $40K-80K/yr |
| **HybridSim Project** | per-project team | floating license pool (5-25 seats) | $200K-1M/yr |
| **HybridSim Academic** | universities, labs | feature-limited (no kanata export, no SimPoint estimate report) | $5K-15K/yr |

Add-ons (post-v1.0):
- Linux/SMP support pack (multi-hart, S/U-mode beyond v1.0 envelope)
- Custom Andes IP variant support (one-off NRE)
- Premium SLA (24h response, dedicated FAE)

### 6.2 License enforcement

- Network license daemon (FlexLM-class) per industry norm
- Node-locked option for air-gapped customers (HSM-bound)
- Floating pool with checkout / checkin
- Per-feature flags (kanata, SimPoint, vendor CSR pack)
- License expiry triggers graceful shutdown with checkpoint export

### 6.3 Delivery channels

- Direct (Andes sales) for top-50 accounts
- Distributor / reseller for long tail (e.g. through Andes regional
  partners in Japan, EU, US)
- Evaluation: 30-day full-feature trial under EULA, node-locked

---

## 7. Market Requirements

Numbered MRs for traceability into FRS.md. Each MR has a status
relative to v1.0 ship.

### MR-A - Cycle-exact ROI measurement on customer workloads

Customer provides their own ELF (closed source). HybridSim
fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.

- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.

### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI

Boot Linux, reach userspace hot loop, hand off to cycle engine,
measure, hand back to QEMU.

- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace
  ship a cycle figure end-to-end.

### MR-C - Whole-program estimate via SimPoint

Long workload, no explicit ROI. SimPoint clustering picks
representative regions, cycle engine measures each, weighted
combine produces a whole-program estimate.

- Acceptance: weighted estimate within 5-10% of fully-RTL on at
  least 3 SPEC-class workloads.

### MR-D - Closed-source RTL protection (encryption)

Cycle engine is RTL-derived (via Verilator) but the shipped binary
must not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch internals.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.

### MR-E - Andes vendor CSR and ACE parity

All customer-visible Andes vendor CSRs and ACE coherence flows
round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite passes 100%; ACE
  coherence regression passes on multi-hart workloads.

### MR-F - Pipeline trace export (kanata)

Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle
window with output byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline.

- Acceptance: kanata diff against fully-RTL baseline is empty for
  the post-warmup window.

### MR-G - Iterative microarch tweak loop

Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
checkpoint without re-running boot.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a
  reference workload.

### MR-H - Multi-hart support

At least 4 harts in the cycle engine with coherent state transport
through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart parallel kernel round-trips and produces a
  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.

### MR-I - Determinism and reproducibility

Identical inputs (ELF + config + seed) produce bit-identical cycle
counts and pipeline traces across runs and hosts.

- Acceptance: a reproducibility test suite runs the same workload
  on 3 different hosts; all outputs bit-identical.

### MR-J - CI / batch integration

The product runs unattended in a CI environment. License daemon,
checkpointing, error reporting, and exit codes are CI-friendly.

- Acceptance: a reference CI pipeline (GitLab / Jenkins) runs 20
  workloads in parallel, collects results, no manual intervention.

### MR-K - First-class observability

Every handoff, trigger, and state transport event is logged with
structured key=value format. Errors are actionable, not "internal
error".

- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a
  log message identifying the corrupted register and the handoff
  phase. No silent failures.

---

## 8. Go-to-Market & Delivery

### 8.1 Design-partner phase (months 0-6 post-engineering complete)

- 3-5 named Andes customers under NDA evaluate pre-GA build
- Free use under design-partner agreement; required to give
  feedback and bug reports
- Goal: prove MR-A + MR-B on real customer workloads before GA

### 8.2 Controlled GA (months 6-12)

- Direct sales to ~10 accounts at full price
- Quarterly feature releases
- Dedicated FAE per top-3 account

### 8.3 Broad GA (year 2+)

- Distributor channel opens
- Academic SKU launches
- Add-on packs (multi-hart, vendor IP variants) release

### 8.4 Onboarding goal

Customer goes from license activation to first valid cycle figure
on their own workload in **under 1 working day** with documentation
alone, no FAE intervention.

---

## 9. Success Metrics

### 9.1 Product KPIs

| Metric | v1.0 target | Year-2 target |
|---|---|---|
| Wall-clock speedup vs vsim-alone (1% ROI workload) | 100x | 1000x |
| Per-ROI accuracy vs fully-RTL | <= 1% | <= 0.5% |
| SimPoint whole-program accuracy | 5-10% | 3-5% |
| Time-to-first-result for new user | 1 day | 2 hours |
| Determinism rate across hosts | 100% bit-identical | 100% bit-identical |

### 9.2 Business KPIs

| Metric | Year-1 | Year-3 |
|---|---|---|
| Paying accounts | 3 | 11 |
| ARR | $300K | $2M-5M |
| Design-partner -> paying conversion | 60% | 75% |
| Customer renewal rate | n/a | >= 80% |
| Net Promoter Score | n/a | >= 30 |

---

## 10. Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Probability | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Encryption tooling adds 6-12 months | ship slip | high | start encryption track in parallel with engineering Wave 1; consider Carbon-style external partner |
| ZeBu price compression for RISC-V mid-market | margin erosion | medium | deepen Andes IP integration; sell on TCO not list price |
| Imperas under Synopsys expands into Andes IP | direct competitor | medium | move first; lock design partners |
| Customer demands ISA beyond Andes | scope creep | medium | charter Andes-only for v1.0; revisit at v2.0 |
| Verilator licensing review for commercial redistribution | legal block | low | LGPL compliance audit before alpha; consider clean-room or commercial Verilator |
| Customer workloads break v1.0 envelope (S/U-mode, paging) | scope gap | high | publish envelope explicitly (FRS); roadmap visible to customer |
| vsim cycle-side too slow for billion-cycle ROIs | win-rate drop | medium | SimPoint coverage; multi-instance parallel measurement |

---

## 11. Roadmap to v1.0

Engineering (from `ROADMAP.md` Track E, formerly `commercial_v1_roadmap.md`):

| Wave | Closes | Cumulative weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Wave 0 | tooling, CI, regression harness | 3 |
| Wave 1 | M-mode loud-failure, basic deliverables | 6 |
| Wave 2 | S/U-mode, paging, traps, PMP (L1-L6) | 18 |
| Wave 3 | Andes vendor CSR, ACE, trigger redesign | 22 |
| Wave 4 | multi-hart (L8) | 26 |
| Wave 5 | SimPoint productization (L14), CI bands | 30 |

Productization (new, parallel track):

| Track | Closes | Weeks |
|---|---|---|
| Encryption pipeline | MR-D | 24-48 |
| License daemon | MR-J | 12 |
| Installer / packaging | section 2 deliverables | 8 |
| Documentation set | section 8 onboarding goal | 12 (continuous) |
| Support tooling (bug capture, telemetry, opt-in) | section 8 | 8 |
| Design-partner program | section 8.1 | continuous |

Critical path: **encryption pipeline** (24-48 weeks). Cannot ship
to customer without it (MR-D).

---

## 12. Open Product Questions

For BU lead and PM review:

- **Pricing**: confirm $40K-80K/seat is acceptable in the Andes
  customer base. Sales has data points.
- **License model**: per-seat vs per-project ratio target?
- **Encryption partner**: build in-house (24-48 weeks) or contract
  (Carbon-style external vendor, faster but adds royalty)?
- **Verilator commercial path**: are we LGPL-clean for
  redistribution, or do we need a commercial Verilator license?
- **First design partners**: which 3-5 accounts get the pre-GA
  build? Sales to propose.
- **Andes-only or RISC-V-broad**: hold v1.0 to Andes ISA only, or
  open the QEMU plugin layer to non-Andes RISC-V from day one?
- **Internal use revenue accounting**: how does internal Andes

---

1	# Hybrid Simulator - Functional Requirements Specification
2	
3	Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-29. Owner: Nick.
4	Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering.
5	
6	Companion to `MRD.md` (commercial product view). This document is
7	the **engineering contract**: every shippable behavior of Andes
8	HybridSim v1.0, with one-line acceptance criteria per requirement.
9	
10	Requirement IDs are stable across drafts. Each FR traces back to
11	one or more MR-x in MRD.md.
12	
13	---
14	
15	## 1. Scope and Definitions
16	
17	### 1.1 In scope
18	
19	Andes HybridSim v1.0, the commercial Tier-2 hybrid simulator
20	described in `MRD.md` sections 1-2. Specifically:
21	
22	- `hsim` driver CLI
23	- QEMU (Andes fork) with hybrid plugin
24	- vsim cycle engine (Verilator-derived, encrypted)
25	- State transport library (`hybrid_state_v1`)
26	- Trigger toolkit (magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint)
27	- Pipeline trace converter (kanata, Clarity DB)
28	- License daemon
29	- Installer, documentation, sample workloads
30	
31	### 1.2 Out of scope (v1.0)
32	
33	- Non-Andes RISC-V ISA variants
34	- QEMU + Alioth (cycle-side Alioth) - documented as future in MRD
35	- FPGA backend
36	- Cloud-hosted SaaS delivery
37	- Multi-cluster cache coherence beyond a single Andes cluster
38	- Vector extension `V` beyond what AndeStar V5 covers
39	
40	### 1.3 Definitions
41	
42	| Term | Definition |
43	|---|---|
44	| ROI | Region of Interest. Window of dynamic instructions to measure cycle-exactly. |
45	| Fast engine | QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin. Runs non-ROI code. |
46	| Cycle engine | vsim, encrypted Verilator-derived binary. Runs ROI. |
47	| Handoff | Atomic state transfer between fast and cycle engine. |
48	| Trigger | A mechanism that fires the handoff (magic-CSR write, PC match, icount expiry, SimPoint marker). |
49	| Hybrid state | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format - GPR, FPR, V-state, CSR, PC, mem snapshot, timing baseline. |
50	| Cycle figure | The cycle count delta across the ROI window, returned to the user. |
51	| Warmup | Initial cycles after handoff where cache/predictor state is not yet steady; excluded from acceptance comparison. |
52	
53	### 1.4 Traceability
54	
55	Every FR includes a `Traces: MR-x [, MR-y...]` line tying it back
56	to `MRD.md`.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## 2. System Architecture Overview
61	
62	```
63	+--------+   trigger   +----------+   handoff   +--------+
64	|  ELF   | ----------> |   QEMU   | ----------> |  vsim  |
65	| (cust) |             |  + plug  |  state +    | cycle  |
66	+--------+             +----------+   mem mmap  | engine |
67	                            ^                   +--------+
68	                            |   handback             |
69	                            +------------------------+
70	                                state + cycle count
71	```
72	
73	Three phases per workload:
74	1. **QEMU1**: boot + setup, fast.
75	2. **vsim**: ROI, cycle-exact, encrypted.
76	3. **QEMU2**: post-ROI, fast (optional, for whole-program runs).
77	
78	Shared substrate: `/dev/shm` mmap-backed RAM, file-descriptor
79	based state transport (`hybrid_state_v1`), license daemon over
80	network socket.
81	
82	---
83	
84	## 3. FR-1xx Functional Capabilities
85	
86	### FR-101 - Three-phase handoff orchestration
87	
88	`hsim run` shall execute the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 sequence
89	without user intervention beyond the initial invocation.
90	
91	- Inputs: ELF, ROI specification (trigger config), workload args
92	- Output: cycle figure (decimal), exit code, optional pipeline trace
93	- Acceptance: a bare-metal kernel with PC-trigger round-trips end-to-end with exit code 0.
94	- Traces: MR-A, MR-G
95	
96	### FR-102 - Trigger: magic-CSR write
97	
98	A write to a configured CSR (default `0x7C0`, customer-configurable)
99	shall fire the QEMU->vsim handoff at the next instruction boundary.
100	
101	- Acceptance: ELF that writes magic-CSR triggers handoff within 1 instruction; no false positives in 1B-cycle stress test.
102	- Traces: MR-A
103	
104	### FR-103 - Trigger: PC watchpoint
105	
106	A configured PC address shall fire the handoff at the matching
107	instruction without requiring source modification.
108	
109	- Acceptance: closed-source ELF (no magic-CSR access) triggers correctly on PC match.
110	- Traces: MR-A, MR-D (closed-source customer ELFs)
111	
112	### FR-104 - Trigger: instruction count
113	
114	A configured icount threshold shall fire the handoff after N
115	dynamic instructions from a reference point.
116	
117	- Acceptance: handoff fires at exactly icount=N, deterministic across runs.
118	- Traces: MR-C, MR-I
119	
120	### FR-105 - Trigger: SimPoint cluster marker
121	
122	The SimPoint clustering tool shall generate a per-cluster trigger
123	spec consumable by `hsim run --mode simpoint`.
124	
125	- Acceptance: SimPoint output drives N handoffs at N cluster boundaries; per-cluster cycle figures collected and weight-combined.
126	- Traces: MR-C
127	
128	### FR-106 - QEMU1 -> vsim handoff: full state transport
129	
130	The following state shall transport bit-exactly from QEMU to vsim:
131	
132	- 32 GPRs (RV64I)
133	- 32 FPRs (with NaN-boxing per RISC-V spec)
134	- V-state (vector regs + vcsr per AndeStar V5)
135	- All architectural CSRs reachable in supported privilege modes
136	- All Andes-vendor CSRs in the customer-visible list (see FR-401)
137	- PC
138	- Memory snapshot (shared mmap RAM)
139	- PMP config (read-only, enforced at vsim entry)
140	- Trap delegation state
141	
142	- Acceptance: post-handoff vsim execution of `nop` produces identical architectural-visible state as a fully-RTL run from the same checkpoint.
143	- Traces: MR-A, MR-E, MR-I
144	
145	### FR-107 - vsim -> QEMU2 handback
146	
147	Symmetric to FR-106. State at vsim ROI exit shall be re-injected
148	into QEMU2 bit-exactly.
149	
150	- Acceptance: bare-metal workload completes execution under QEMU2 after a vsim ROI window; final result matches fully-RTL baseline.
151	- Traces: MR-A, MR-G
152	
153	### FR-108 - M-mode workload support
154	
155	The v1.0 envelope shall include any RV64GC + AndeStar V5 workload
156	running entirely in M-mode with PMP-static, trap-free ROI.
157	
158	- Acceptance: 10 representative M-mode kernels round-trip without error.
159	- Traces: MR-A
160	
161	### FR-109 - S-mode and U-mode workload support
162	
163	The v1.0 envelope shall extend to S-mode and U-mode workloads,
164	including supervisor page tables (Sv39/Sv48) and trap handling
165	inside the ROI.
166	
167	- Acceptance: 3 Linux userspace workloads (SPEC-class) round-trip.
168	- Traces: MR-B
169	
170	### FR-110 - Cycle figure reporting
171	
172	After every successful run, `hsim` shall emit:
173	- Total ROI cycles (decimal)
174	- Per-phase wall-clock time
175	- SimPoint weighted estimate (when applicable)
176	- Confidence band on the estimate (95% CI)
177	
178	- Acceptance: machine-parseable JSON report at `hsim.report.json`.
179	- Traces: MR-C, MR-J
180	
181	### FR-111 - Pipeline trace export: kanata
182	
183	When `--trace kanata` is set, the cycle engine shall emit kanata
184	format for the ROI window, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline
185	after warmup.
186	
187	- Acceptance: `diff` against fully-RTL kanata is empty for the post-warmup window.
188	- Traces: MR-F
189	
190	### FR-112 - Pipeline trace export: Clarity DB
191	
192	When `--trace clarity` is set, the cycle engine shall emit a
193	Clarity-format pipeline DB for the ROI window.
194	
195	- Acceptance: Clarity DB import into the Andes Clarity viewer succeeds; per-stage event counts match fully-RTL.
196	- Traces: MR-F
197	
198	### FR-113 - Multi-hart ROI
199	
200	`hsim` shall support ROIs that span >= 4 harts with coherent state
201	transport through ACE.
202	
203	- Acceptance: a 4-hart kernel round-trips; cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
204	- Traces: MR-H
205	
206	### FR-114 - Resumable / checkpointed runs
207	
208	A long QEMU1 phase shall be checkpointable mid-run, so a customer
209	can boot once and re-enter vsim multiple times without re-booting.
210	
211	- Acceptance: customer boots Linux once (~30 min), then runs 10
212	  different ROIs measured against the same checkpoint, with total
213	  wall-clock under 1 hour.
214	- Traces: MR-G
215	
216	---
217	
218	## 4. FR-2xx Performance Requirements
219	
220	### FR-201 - Wall-clock speedup envelope
221	
222	On a workload where the ROI is <= 1% of dynamic instructions,
223	HybridSim shall complete in <= 1% of the wall-clock time of a
224	vsim-alone run of the same workload.
225	
226	- Acceptance: 3 reference workloads measured; speedup >= 100x.
227	- Traces: MR-A, MRD section 9.1
228	
229	### FR-202 - Per-ROI accuracy
230	
231	The cycle figure for the ROI window shall agree with a fully-RTL
232	baseline within 1% after a documented warmup tolerance.
233	
234	- Acceptance: 5 reference ROIs; max error <= 1.0%.
235	- Traces: MR-A, MR-E
236	
237	### FR-203 - SimPoint whole-program accuracy
238	
239	The weighted whole-program estimate from SimPoint mode shall be
240	within 5-10% of fully-RTL on SPEC-class workloads.
241	
242	- Acceptance: 3 SPEC-class workloads; max error <= 10%, average <= 5%.
243	- Traces: MR-C
244	
245	### FR-204 - Time-to-first-result
246	
247	A new customer with the installer and a sample workload shall
248	produce a valid cycle figure within 1 working day, with
249	documentation alone (no FAE involvement).
250	
251	- Acceptance: timed user study with 3 fresh engineers; 100% reach valid figure within 8 hours.
252	- Traces: MRD section 8.4
253	
254	### FR-205 - Iterative re-measurement latency
255	
256	After an initial QEMU1 phase, a re-measurement of the same ROI
257	with an updated cycle engine shall complete in <= 5 minutes.
258	
259	- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle measured on 3 microarch parameter tweaks.
260	- Traces: MR-G
261	
262	---
263	
264	## 5. FR-3xx Interface Requirements
265	
266	### FR-301 - `hsim` CLI
267	
268	Top-level entry. Subcommands:
269	- `hsim run` - one-shot workload execution
270	- `hsim simpoint` - clustering + per-cluster runs + combine
271	- `hsim trace` - trace-only mode (kanata, clarity)
272	- `hsim checkpoint` - QEMU1 checkpoint management
273	- `hsim license` - license daemon control / diagnostics
274	- `hsim diag` - capture bug report bundle
275	- `hsim version` - prints versions of all components
276	
277	- Acceptance: `--help` for every subcommand; exit codes per Unix convention.
278	- Traces: MR-J, MR-K
279	
280	### FR-302 - Configuration file format
281	
282	`hsim.config.yaml` shall specify trigger config, workload paths,
283	cycle-engine params, license server, output format. Schema-validated.
284	
285	- Acceptance: bad config produces actionable error pointing at the offending line.
286	- Traces: MR-J, MR-K
287	
288	### FR-303 - JSON output report
289	
290	Every run shall emit `hsim.report.json` with the schema defined in
291	`docs/report-schema.json` (to be written).
292	
293	- Acceptance: schema validation passes on every successful run.
294	- Traces: MR-J
295	
296	### FR-304 - Programmatic API (Python binding)
297	
298	A Python module shall expose the `hsim run` interface as a function
299	returning the report dict. For CI scripting.
300	
301	- Acceptance: `import hsim; r = hsim.run(...)` returns a parsed report.
302	- Traces: MR-J
303	
304	### FR-305 - Exit codes
305	
306	| Code | Meaning |
307	|---|---|
308	| 0 | run succeeded, valid cycle figure |
309	| 1 | configuration error |
310	| 2 | license error |
311	| 3 | trigger never fired |
312	| 4 | state-transport corruption detected |
313	| 5 | cycle engine crashed |
314	| 6 | QEMU engine crashed |
315	| 7 | ROI exited unexpectedly |
316	| 9x | reserved |
317	
318	- Acceptance: each documented failure produces the matching exit code in a fault-injection test.
319	- Traces: MR-J, MR-K
320	
321	---
322	
323	## 6. FR-4xx Compatibility Requirements
324	
325	### FR-401 - Andes IP coverage
326	
327	v1.0 shall support these Andes cores: AX25, AX27, AX45, AX46.
328	D23v deferred to v1.1.
329	
330	For each core, the Andes vendor CSR set published in the AndeStar
331	V5 specification (revision frozen at v1.0 ship) shall round-trip
332	bit-exactly.
333	
334	- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite (~50 CSRs per core) passes 100%.
335	- Traces: MR-E
336	
337	### FR-402 - ACE coherence support
338	
339	Multi-hart workloads shall transport ACE coherence state
340	(directory + snoop filter) bit-exactly across the handoff.
341	
342	- Acceptance: a coherent multi-hart test (e.g. shared-counter benchmark) produces identical results to fully-RTL.
343	- Traces: MR-E, MR-H
344	
345	### FR-403 - Host OS support
346	
347	v1.0 ships for x86_64 Linux only. Supported distros: Ubuntu 22.04
348	LTS, RHEL 8 and 9, SUSE SLES 15. No Windows, no macOS.
349	
350	- Acceptance: install + smoke test passes on each supported distro.
351	- Traces: MRD section 8
352	
353	### FR-404 - Toolchain compatibility
354	
355	ELFs produced by:
356	- Andes GNU toolchain (current and previous release)
357	- Andes LLVM toolchain (current release)
358	- Upstream RISC-V GCC (current release)
359	
360	shall be accepted.
361	
362	- Acceptance: a benchmark built with each toolchain round-trips.
363	- Traces: MR-A
364	
365	### FR-405 - QEMU upstream tracking
366	
367	The QEMU engine shall be based on QEMU 9.x, with documented
368	patch set against upstream. Customer can rebuild from source under
369	NDA (source escrow).
370	
371	- Acceptance: source tarball + patch series builds against upstream 9.x.
372	- Traces: MRD section 12 (QEMU dependency)
373	
374	---
375	
376	## 7. FR-5xx IP Protection Requirements
377	
378	### FR-501 - Cycle-engine binary encryption
379	
380	The vsim binary shall not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch
381	internals by static or dynamic analysis.
382	
383	- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit; legal sign-off.
384	- Traces: MR-D
385	
386	### FR-502 - Anti-debug / anti-instrumentation
387	
388	The cycle engine shall refuse to execute under `ptrace`, `gdb`,
389	`strace`, dynamic tracing, or memory-introspection tools beyond
390	those explicitly whitelisted for support telemetry.
391	
392	- Acceptance: attempted attach produces an actionable refusal log; no crash, no leak.
393	- Traces: MR-D
394	
395	### FR-503 - State-transport encryption
396	
397	`hybrid_state_v1` payload in `/dev/shm` shall be encrypted at rest
398	with a session key derived from license activation. Plaintext
399	visible only within the cycle engine address space.
400	
401	- Acceptance: external readers of `/dev/shm` see ciphertext; the cycle engine reads it correctly.
402	- Traces: MR-D
403	
404	### FR-504 - License key binding
405	
406	The cycle engine binary shall refuse to execute without a valid
407	license check-out from the license daemon. License key is bound to
408	host MAC + HSM (node-locked) or floating pool (network).
409	
410	- Acceptance: missing or invalid license produces exit code 2 with a clear message.
411	- Traces: MR-J, MRD section 6.2
412	
413	### FR-505 - License feature flags
414	
415	License records shall carry per-feature flags:
416	- core support pack (which Andes cores)
417	- kanata export
418	- SimPoint
419	- multi-hart
420	- premium SLA (telemetry-routed)
421	
422	Cycle engine shall enforce flags at runtime.
423	
424	- Acceptance: a license without kanata flag refuses `--trace kanata` with exit 2.
425	- Traces: MRD section 6.2
426	
427	### FR-506 - License expiry
428	
429	License expiry shall:
430	1. Refuse new runs (exit code 2).
431	2. Allow in-progress runs to complete with a warning log.
432	3. Not corrupt or drop reports already written to disk.
433	
434	- Acceptance: clock-skew test (advance host clock past expiry mid-run) shows graceful behavior per spec.
435	- Traces: MRD section 6.2
436	
437	### FR-507 - Source escrow
438	
439	For top-tier customers, source for the cycle engine shall be
440	deposited with a neutral escrow agent and released on documented
441	trigger events (e.g. Andes EOL of the product).
442	
443	- Acceptance: escrow agreement signed; release procedure documented.
444	- Traces: MRD section 12
445	
446	---
447	
448	## 8. FR-6xx Quality & Observability
449	
450	### FR-601 - Structured logging
451	
452	Every internal event (trigger fire, handoff begin/end, state
453	transport, license check, error) shall log in the format
454	`[Tag] evt=<ns>.<action> key=value ...`.
455	
456	- Acceptance: a regex-based log validator passes on a sample run.
457	- Traces: MR-K
458	
459	### FR-602 - Log levels
460	
461	Log levels: ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE. Default INFO. Settable
462	via `--log-level` or `HSIM_LOG_LEVEL` env.
463	
464	- Acceptance: level filtering observable on a sample run.
465	- Traces: MR-K
466	
467	### FR-603 - Bug report bundle
468	
469	`hsim diag` shall capture:
470	- All log files
471	- The active config
472	- The `hybrid_state_v1` snapshot (encrypted, support-only readable)
473	- Host info (uname, distro, libc, kernel, license daemon state)
474	- Reproducer ELF and config (with customer opt-in)
475	
476	into a single tarball ready to attach to a support ticket.
477	
478	- Acceptance: support reproduces a customer-reported bug from a `hsim diag` bundle alone.
479	- Traces: MR-K
480	
481	### FR-604 - Deterministic mode
482	
483	When `--deterministic` is set, every run with the same inputs
484	produces bit-identical cycle figure, pipeline trace, and report
485	across hosts and runs.
486	
487	- Acceptance: cross-host reproducibility test (3 hosts) passes.
488	- Traces: MR-I
489	
490	### FR-605 - Error message quality bar
491	
492	Every fatal error shall include:
493	- a unique error code (e.g. `HSIM-E0042`)
494	- a one-line description
495	- a pointer to the doc section that explains it
496	- the suspected failing component
497	- recommended next step (retry, contact support, check config)
498	
499	- Acceptance: a sample of 20 deliberate errors are graded against the bar; >= 90% pass.
500	- Traces: MR-K
501	
502	### FR-606 - Telemetry (opt-in)
503	
504	With explicit customer opt-in, `hsim` may transmit anonymized
505	usage data (workload size, success/failure code, host info) to
506	Andes telemetry endpoint. Default off.
507	
508	- Acceptance: telemetry disabled by default; opt-in via config flag; payload schema documented and signed-off by legal.
509	- Traces: MRD section 8
510	
511	---
512	
513	## 9. FR-7xx Packaging & Delivery
514	
515	### FR-701 - Installer
516	
517	A single self-extracting installer (`.run` or `.deb` / `.rpm`)
518	shall install all components into a configurable prefix, register
519	the license daemon, and run a post-install smoke test.
520	
521	- Acceptance: fresh-host install on each supported distro completes in <= 5 minutes and passes the smoke test.
522	- Traces: MRD section 8
523	
524	### FR-702 - Dependency footprint
525	
526	The installer shall declare all external runtime dependencies.
527	Anything not in the base distro must be bundled.
528	
529	- Acceptance: dependency audit passes; no surprise yum/apt requirements at runtime.
530	- Traces: MRD section 8
531	
532	### FR-703 - Upgrade in place
533	
534	A version N+1 installer over version N shall preserve config,
535	license, and existing checkpoints; report any incompatibilities
536	explicitly.
537	
538	- Acceptance: N -> N+1 upgrade test on each supported distro; checkpoints from N work on N+1 or produce a documented error.
539	- Traces: MR-G, MRD section 8
540	
541	### FR-704 - Uninstaller
542	
543	Clean uninstall shall remove all installed files, license records,
544	and daemons. User-generated data (reports, checkpoints) preserved
545	unless explicitly removed.
546	
547	- Acceptance: post-uninstall, no `hsim` binaries on path; no daemons running.
548	- Traces: MRD section 8
549	
550	### FR-705 - Documentation set
551	
552	Shipped with installer:
553	- Installation guide
554	- User guide (mirrors `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`)
555	- ABI reference (`hybrid_state_v1`, trigger spec, report schema)
556	- Integration guide (CI, Python API)
557	- Limitations document (current envelope from `limitation.md`)
558	- Error code reference (from FR-605)
559	- Release notes per version
560	
561	- Acceptance: documentation review by an external technical writer signs off readability.
562	- Traces: MRD section 8.4
563	
564	---
565	
566	## 10. FR-8xx Support & Lifecycle
567	
568	### FR-801 - Versioning
569	
570	Semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. ABI breaks bump MAJOR.
571	
572	- Acceptance: version policy documented; any ABI break is gated by a code review checklist.
573	- Traces: MRD section 8
574	
575	### FR-802 - Support tiers
576	
577	| Tier | Response | Channels |
578	|---|---|---|
579	| Standard | 3 business days | email, web ticket |
580	| Premium | 1 business day | email, web ticket, named FAE |
581	| Mission Critical | 4 hours | phone, dedicated FAE, war-room access |
582	
583	- Acceptance: each tier has a documented SLA and escalation path.
584	- Traces: MRD section 6.1
585	
586	### FR-803 - EOL policy
587	
588	Each MAJOR version shall be supported for >= 3 years from GA; EOL
589	announced >= 12 months in advance.
590	
591	- Acceptance: EOL policy published; reflected in license terms.
592	- Traces: MRD section 8
593	
594	### FR-804 - Patch release cadence
595	
596	PATCH releases every 4 weeks for v1.0; MINOR releases every quarter.
597	
598	- Acceptance: release cadence documented and trackable in CI.
599	- Traces: MRD section 8.2
600	
601	---
602	
603	## 11. FR-9xx Security & Compliance
604	
605	### FR-901 - License server security
606	
607	The license daemon shall:
608	- TLS 1.3 for all network communication
609	- HSM-bound private keys
610	- Logged audit trail of every check-out / check-in
611	
612	- Acceptance: third-party security audit; OWASP Top 10 review.
613	- Traces: MRD section 6.2
614	
615	### FR-902 - Open-source compliance
616	
617	For every OSS component shipped, the installer shall include:
618	- License text
619	- Source pointer (URL or escrow)
620	- Modification disclosure (for LGPL components like Verilator)
621	
622	- Acceptance: OSS compliance audit by Andes legal.
623	- Traces: MRD section 10 (Verilator licensing review)
624	
625	### FR-903 - Export control
626	
627	Product classification reviewed for US EAR / ITAR; documented ECCN.
628	Installer enforces destination country checks where required.
629	
630	- Acceptance: export control review by Andes legal; ECCN documented in product sheet.
631	- Traces: MRD section 6.3
632	
633	### FR-904 - Supply chain integrity
634	
635	All shipped binaries shall be signed with an Andes code-signing
636	certificate. Installer verifies signatures before extraction.
637	
638	- Acceptance: signature verification on every install; tampered installer is refused with a clear message.
639	- Traces: MR-D, MR-K
640	
641	---
642	
643	## 12. Acceptance Test Matrix
644	
645	Mapping FR to test suites. Each test suite is owned by a named
646	engineer; pass/fail tracked in CI dashboard before any release.
647	
648	| Suite | Covers | Owner |
649	|---|---|---|
650	| smoke | FR-101, FR-204, FR-701, FR-702 | tbd |
651	| state-transport | FR-106, FR-107, FR-401, FR-402 | tbd |
652	| trigger | FR-102, FR-103, FR-104, FR-105 | tbd |
653	| accuracy | FR-202, FR-203 | tbd |
654	| simpoint | FR-105, FR-203 | tbd |
655	| multi-hart | FR-113, FR-402 | tbd |
656	| trace | FR-111, FR-112 | tbd |
657	| determinism | FR-604, FR-203 | tbd |
658	| license | FR-504, FR-505, FR-506 | tbd |
659	| ip-protection | FR-501, FR-502, FR-503 | tbd |
660	| installer | FR-701, FR-702, FR-703, FR-704 | tbd |
661	| docs | FR-705 | tbd |
662	| security | FR-901, FR-902, FR-903, FR-904 | tbd |
663	
664	---
665	
666	## 13. Traceability Matrix (MR -> FR)
667	
668	| MR | Description | FRs |
669	|---|---|---|
670	| MR-A | Cycle-exact ROI on customer workloads | FR-101, FR-102, FR-103, FR-106, FR-108, FR-202, FR-404 |
671	| MR-B | Linux + userspace ROI | FR-109 |
672	| MR-C | Whole-program estimate via SimPoint | FR-104, FR-105, FR-110, FR-203 |
673	| MR-D | RTL protection / encryption | FR-501, FR-502, FR-503, FR-904 |
674	| MR-E | Andes vendor CSR + ACE parity | FR-401, FR-402, FR-106 |
675	| MR-F | Pipeline trace export | FR-111, FR-112 |
676	| MR-G | Iterative microarch tweak | FR-101, FR-114, FR-205, FR-703 |
677	| MR-H | Multi-hart | FR-113, FR-402 |
678	| MR-I | Determinism | FR-104, FR-106, FR-604 |
679	| MR-J | CI / batch integration | FR-301, FR-302, FR-303, FR-304, FR-305, FR-504, FR-606 |
680	| MR-K | First-class observability | FR-601, FR-602, FR-603, FR-605, FR-904 |
681	
682	Every MR has at least 2 supporting FRs. Every FR traces back to
683	at least one MR. No orphan requirements.
684	
685	---
686	
687	## 14. Open Engineering Questions
688	
689	For Engineering / IP officer review:
690	
691	- **Encryption mechanism**: in-house obfuscation pass on Verilator
692	  output, or external Carbon-style partner? Trade-off:
693	  build-vs-buy, royalty vs salary, time-to-market.
694	- **License daemon**: build on FlexLM (industry standard but
695	  licensing fee), Reprise RLM, or in-house? FlexLM has highest
696	  customer acceptance.
697	- **State-transport encryption key**: derive from license daemon
698	  on each run, or fixed per install? Per-run is more secure but
699	  adds latency.
700	- **vsim binary size**: encrypted output is typically 2-5x source
701	  size; what is the acceptable footprint?
702	- **Multi-hart determinism**: scheduling order in vsim cycle engine
703	  is deterministic given seed; QEMU side may not be. Strategy?
704	- **Vendor CSR list**: FR-401 says "published in AndeStar V5"; need
705	  a frozen list per core for the v1.0 commit.
706	- **Source escrow**: which neutral agent (Iron Mountain, NCC, etc)
707	  and what are the customer-facing trigger conditions?
708	
709	---
710	
711	## 15. References
712	
713	- `MRD.md` - commercial market requirements
714	- `ROADMAP.md` - master feature roadmap (engineering plan; supersedes
715	  `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md`)
716	- `docs/limitation.md` - current envelope
717	- `hybrid_plan.md` - architecture and rationale
718	- `docs/USER_GUIDE.md` - user-facing workflow doc
719	- AndeStar V5 specification (vendor CSR list source of truth)
720	- Verilator commercial use guidelines (LGPL review)
721	- FlexLM and Reprise RLM documentation (license daemon options)

# Hybrid Simulator - Functional Requirements Specification

Status: draft v0.1. Written 2026-05-29. Owner: Nick.
Audience: Engineering, QA, IP/Legal, Sales engineering.

Companion to `MRD.md` (commercial product view). This document is
the **engineering contract**: every shippable behavior of Andes
HybridSim v1.0, with one-line acceptance criteria per requirement.

Requirement IDs are stable across drafts. Each FR traces back to
one or more MR-x in MRD.md.

---

## 1. Scope and Definitions

### 1.1 In scope

Andes HybridSim v1.0, the commercial Tier-2 hybrid simulator
described in `MRD.md` sections 1-2. Specifically:

- `hsim` driver CLI
- QEMU (Andes fork) with hybrid plugin
- vsim cycle engine (Verilator-derived, encrypted)
- State transport library (`hybrid_state_v1`)
- Trigger toolkit (magic-CSR, PC-watch, icount, SimPoint)
- Pipeline trace converter (kanata, Clarity DB)
- License daemon
- Installer, documentation, sample workloads

### 1.2 Out of scope (v1.0)

- Non-Andes RISC-V ISA variants
- QEMU + Alioth (cycle-side Alioth) - documented as future in MRD
- FPGA backend
- Cloud-hosted SaaS delivery
- Multi-cluster cache coherence beyond a single Andes cluster
- Vector extension `V` beyond what AndeStar V5 covers

### 1.3 Definitions

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| ROI | Region of Interest. Window of dynamic instructions to measure cycle-exactly. |
| Fast engine | QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin. Runs non-ROI code. |
| Cycle engine | vsim, encrypted Verilator-derived binary. Runs ROI. |
| Handoff | Atomic state transfer between fast and cycle engine. |
| Trigger | A mechanism that fires the handoff (magic-CSR write, PC match, icount expiry, SimPoint marker). |
| Hybrid state | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format - GPR, FPR, V-state, CSR, PC, mem snapshot, timing baseline. |
| Cycle figure | The cycle count delta across the ROI window, returned to the user. |
| Warmup | Initial cycles after handoff where cache/predictor state is not yet steady; excluded from acceptance comparison. |

### 1.4 Traceability

Every FR includes a `Traces: MR-x [, MR-y...]` line tying it back
to `MRD.md`.

---

## 2. System Architecture Overview

```
+--------+   trigger   +----------+   handoff   +--------+
|  ELF   | ----------> |   QEMU   | ----------> |  vsim  |
| (cust) |             |  + plug  |  state +    | cycle  |
+--------+             +----------+   mem mmap  | engine |
                            ^                   +--------+
                            |   handback             |
                            +------------------------+
                                state + cycle count
```

Three phases per workload:
1. **QEMU1**: boot + setup, fast.
2. **vsim**: ROI, cycle-exact, encrypted.
3. **QEMU2**: post-ROI, fast (optional, for whole-program runs).

Shared substrate: `/dev/shm` mmap-backed RAM, file-descriptor
based state transport (`hybrid_state_v1`), license daemon over
network socket.

---

## 3. FR-1xx Functional Capabilities

### FR-101 - Three-phase handoff orchestration

`hsim run` shall execute the QEMU1 -> vsim -> QEMU2 sequence
without user intervention beyond the initial invocation.

- Inputs: ELF, ROI specification (trigger config), workload args
- Output: cycle figure (decimal), exit code, optional pipeline trace
- Acceptance: a bare-metal kernel with PC-trigger round-trips end-to-end with exit code 0.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-G

### FR-102 - Trigger: magic-CSR write

A write to a configured CSR (default `0x7C0`, customer-configurable)
shall fire the QEMU->vsim handoff at the next instruction boundary.

- Acceptance: ELF that writes magic-CSR triggers handoff within 1 instruction; no false positives in 1B-cycle stress test.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-103 - Trigger: PC watchpoint

A configured PC address shall fire the handoff at the matching
instruction without requiring source modification.

- Acceptance: closed-source ELF (no magic-CSR access) triggers correctly on PC match.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-D (closed-source customer ELFs)

### FR-104 - Trigger: instruction count

A configured icount threshold shall fire the handoff after N
dynamic instructions from a reference point.

- Acceptance: handoff fires at exactly icount=N, deterministic across runs.
- Traces: MR-C, MR-I

### FR-105 - Trigger: SimPoint cluster marker

The SimPoint clustering tool shall generate a per-cluster trigger
spec consumable by `hsim run --mode simpoint`.

- Acceptance: SimPoint output drives N handoffs at N cluster boundaries; per-cluster cycle figures collected and weight-combined.
- Traces: MR-C

### FR-106 - QEMU1 -> vsim handoff: full state transport

The following state shall transport bit-exactly from QEMU to vsim:

- 32 GPRs (RV64I)
- 32 FPRs (with NaN-boxing per RISC-V spec)
- V-state (vector regs + vcsr per AndeStar V5)
- All architectural CSRs reachable in supported privilege modes
- All Andes-vendor CSRs in the customer-visible list (see FR-401)
- PC
- Memory snapshot (shared mmap RAM)
- PMP config (read-only, enforced at vsim entry)
- Trap delegation state

- Acceptance: post-handoff vsim execution of `nop` produces identical architectural-visible state as a fully-RTL run from the same checkpoint.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-E, MR-I

### FR-107 - vsim -> QEMU2 handback

Symmetric to FR-106. State at vsim ROI exit shall be re-injected
into QEMU2 bit-exactly.

- Acceptance: bare-metal workload completes execution under QEMU2 after a vsim ROI window; final result matches fully-RTL baseline.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-G

### FR-108 - M-mode workload support

The v1.0 envelope shall include any RV64GC + AndeStar V5 workload
running entirely in M-mode with PMP-static, trap-free ROI.

- Acceptance: 10 representative M-mode kernels round-trip without error.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-109 - S-mode and U-mode workload support

The v1.0 envelope shall extend to S-mode and U-mode workloads,
including supervisor page tables (Sv39/Sv48) and trap handling
inside the ROI.

- Acceptance: 3 Linux userspace workloads (SPEC-class) round-trip.
- Traces: MR-B

### FR-110 - Cycle figure reporting

After every successful run, `hsim` shall emit:
- Total ROI cycles (decimal)
- Per-phase wall-clock time
- SimPoint weighted estimate (when applicable)
- Confidence band on the estimate (95% CI)

- Acceptance: machine-parseable JSON report at `hsim.report.json`.
- Traces: MR-C, MR-J

### FR-111 - Pipeline trace export: kanata

When `--trace kanata` is set, the cycle engine shall emit kanata
format for the ROI window, byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline
after warmup.

- Acceptance: `diff` against fully-RTL kanata is empty for the post-warmup window.
- Traces: MR-F

### FR-112 - Pipeline trace export: Clarity DB

When `--trace clarity` is set, the cycle engine shall emit a
Clarity-format pipeline DB for the ROI window.

- Acceptance: Clarity DB import into the Andes Clarity viewer succeeds; per-stage event counts match fully-RTL.
- Traces: MR-F

### FR-113 - Multi-hart ROI

`hsim` shall support ROIs that span >= 4 harts with coherent state
transport through ACE.

- Acceptance: a 4-hart kernel round-trips; cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
- Traces: MR-H

### FR-114 - Resumable / checkpointed runs

A long QEMU1 phase shall be checkpointable mid-run, so a customer
can boot once and re-enter vsim multiple times without re-booting.

- Acceptance: customer boots Linux once (~30 min), then runs 10
  different ROIs measured against the same checkpoint, with total
  wall-clock under 1 hour.
- Traces: MR-G

---

## 4. FR-2xx Performance Requirements

### FR-201 - Wall-clock speedup envelope

On a workload where the ROI is <= 1% of dynamic instructions,
HybridSim shall complete in <= 1% of the wall-clock time of a
vsim-alone run of the same workload.

- Acceptance: 3 reference workloads measured; speedup >= 100x.
- Traces: MR-A, MRD section 9.1

### FR-202 - Per-ROI accuracy

The cycle figure for the ROI window shall agree with a fully-RTL
baseline within 1% after a documented warmup tolerance.

- Acceptance: 5 reference ROIs; max error <= 1.0%.
- Traces: MR-A, MR-E

### FR-203 - SimPoint whole-program accuracy

The weighted whole-program estimate from SimPoint mode shall be
within 5-10% of fully-RTL on SPEC-class workloads.

- Acceptance: 3 SPEC-class workloads; max error <= 10%, average <= 5%.
- Traces: MR-C

### FR-204 - Time-to-first-result

A new customer with the installer and a sample workload shall
produce a valid cycle figure within 1 working day, with
documentation alone (no FAE involvement).

- Acceptance: timed user study with 3 fresh engineers; 100% reach valid figure within 8 hours.
- Traces: MRD section 8.4

### FR-205 - Iterative re-measurement latency

After an initial QEMU1 phase, a re-measurement of the same ROI
with an updated cycle engine shall complete in <= 5 minutes.

- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle measured on 3 microarch parameter tweaks.
- Traces: MR-G

---

## 5. FR-3xx Interface Requirements

### FR-301 - `hsim` CLI

Top-level entry. Subcommands:
- `hsim run` - one-shot workload execution
- `hsim simpoint` - clustering + per-cluster runs + combine
- `hsim trace` - trace-only mode (kanata, clarity)
- `hsim checkpoint` - QEMU1 checkpoint management
- `hsim license` - license daemon control / diagnostics
- `hsim diag` - capture bug report bundle
- `hsim version` - prints versions of all components

- Acceptance: `--help` for every subcommand; exit codes per Unix convention.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

### FR-302 - Configuration file format

`hsim.config.yaml` shall specify trigger config, workload paths,
cycle-engine params, license server, output format. Schema-validated.

- Acceptance: bad config produces actionable error pointing at the offending line.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

### FR-303 - JSON output report

Every run shall emit `hsim.report.json` with the schema defined in
`docs/report-schema.json` (to be written).

- Acceptance: schema validation passes on every successful run.
- Traces: MR-J

### FR-304 - Programmatic API (Python binding)

A Python module shall expose the `hsim run` interface as a function
returning the report dict. For CI scripting.

- Acceptance: `import hsim; r = hsim.run(...)` returns a parsed report.
- Traces: MR-J

### FR-305 - Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | run succeeded, valid cycle figure |
| 1 | configuration error |
| 2 | license error |
| 3 | trigger never fired |
| 4 | state-transport corruption detected |
| 5 | cycle engine crashed |
| 6 | QEMU engine crashed |
| 7 | ROI exited unexpectedly |
| 9x | reserved |

- Acceptance: each documented failure produces the matching exit code in a fault-injection test.
- Traces: MR-J, MR-K

---

## 6. FR-4xx Compatibility Requirements

### FR-401 - Andes IP coverage

v1.0 shall support these Andes cores: AX25, AX27, AX45, AX46.
D23v deferred to v1.1.

For each core, the Andes vendor CSR set published in the AndeStar
V5 specification (revision frozen at v1.0 ship) shall round-trip
bit-exactly.

- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite (~50 CSRs per core) passes 100%.
- Traces: MR-E

### FR-402 - ACE coherence support

Multi-hart workloads shall transport ACE coherence state
(directory + snoop filter) bit-exactly across the handoff.

- Acceptance: a coherent multi-hart test (e.g. shared-counter benchmark) produces identical results to fully-RTL.
- Traces: MR-E, MR-H

### FR-403 - Host OS support

v1.0 ships for x86_64 Linux only. Supported distros: Ubuntu 22.04
LTS, RHEL 8 and 9, SUSE SLES 15. No Windows, no macOS.

- Acceptance: install + smoke test passes on each supported distro.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-404 - Toolchain compatibility

ELFs produced by:
- Andes GNU toolchain (current and previous release)
- Andes LLVM toolchain (current release)
- Upstream RISC-V GCC (current release)

shall be accepted.

- Acceptance: a benchmark built with each toolchain round-trips.
- Traces: MR-A

### FR-405 - QEMU upstream tracking

The QEMU engine shall be based on QEMU 9.x, with documented
patch set against upstream. Customer can rebuild from source under
NDA (source escrow).

- Acceptance: source tarball + patch series builds against upstream 9.x.
- Traces: MRD section 12 (QEMU dependency)

---

## 7. FR-5xx IP Protection Requirements

### FR-501 - Cycle-engine binary encryption

The vsim binary shall not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch
internals by static or dynamic analysis.

- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit; legal sign-off.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-502 - Anti-debug / anti-instrumentation

The cycle engine shall refuse to execute under `ptrace`, `gdb`,
`strace`, dynamic tracing, or memory-introspection tools beyond
those explicitly whitelisted for support telemetry.

- Acceptance: attempted attach produces an actionable refusal log; no crash, no leak.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-503 - State-transport encryption

`hybrid_state_v1` payload in `/dev/shm` shall be encrypted at rest
with a session key derived from license activation. Plaintext
visible only within the cycle engine address space.

- Acceptance: external readers of `/dev/shm` see ciphertext; the cycle engine reads it correctly.
- Traces: MR-D

### FR-504 - License key binding

The cycle engine binary shall refuse to execute without a valid
license check-out from the license daemon. License key is bound to
host MAC + HSM (node-locked) or floating pool (network).

- Acceptance: missing or invalid license produces exit code 2 with a clear message.
- Traces: MR-J, MRD section 6.2

### FR-505 - License feature flags

License records shall carry per-feature flags:
- core support pack (which Andes cores)
- kanata export
- SimPoint
- multi-hart
- premium SLA (telemetry-routed)

Cycle engine shall enforce flags at runtime.

- Acceptance: a license without kanata flag refuses `--trace kanata` with exit 2.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-506 - License expiry

License expiry shall:
1. Refuse new runs (exit code 2).
2. Allow in-progress runs to complete with a warning log.
3. Not corrupt or drop reports already written to disk.

- Acceptance: clock-skew test (advance host clock past expiry mid-run) shows graceful behavior per spec.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-507 - Source escrow

For top-tier customers, source for the cycle engine shall be
deposited with a neutral escrow agent and released on documented
trigger events (e.g. Andes EOL of the product).

- Acceptance: escrow agreement signed; release procedure documented.
- Traces: MRD section 12

---

## 8. FR-6xx Quality & Observability

### FR-601 - Structured logging

Every internal event (trigger fire, handoff begin/end, state
transport, license check, error) shall log in the format
`[Tag] evt=<ns>.<action> key=value ...`.

- Acceptance: a regex-based log validator passes on a sample run.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-602 - Log levels

Log levels: ERROR, WARN, INFO, DEBUG, TRACE. Default INFO. Settable
via `--log-level` or `HSIM_LOG_LEVEL` env.

- Acceptance: level filtering observable on a sample run.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-603 - Bug report bundle

`hsim diag` shall capture:
- All log files
- The active config
- The `hybrid_state_v1` snapshot (encrypted, support-only readable)
- Host info (uname, distro, libc, kernel, license daemon state)
- Reproducer ELF and config (with customer opt-in)

into a single tarball ready to attach to a support ticket.

- Acceptance: support reproduces a customer-reported bug from a `hsim diag` bundle alone.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-604 - Deterministic mode

When `--deterministic` is set, every run with the same inputs
produces bit-identical cycle figure, pipeline trace, and report
across hosts and runs.

- Acceptance: cross-host reproducibility test (3 hosts) passes.
- Traces: MR-I

### FR-605 - Error message quality bar

Every fatal error shall include:
- a unique error code (e.g. `HSIM-E0042`)
- a one-line description
- a pointer to the doc section that explains it
- the suspected failing component
- recommended next step (retry, contact support, check config)

- Acceptance: a sample of 20 deliberate errors are graded against the bar; >= 90% pass.
- Traces: MR-K

### FR-606 - Telemetry (opt-in)

With explicit customer opt-in, `hsim` may transmit anonymized
usage data (workload size, success/failure code, host info) to
Andes telemetry endpoint. Default off.

- Acceptance: telemetry disabled by default; opt-in via config flag; payload schema documented and signed-off by legal.
- Traces: MRD section 8

---

## 9. FR-7xx Packaging & Delivery

### FR-701 - Installer

A single self-extracting installer (`.run` or `.deb` / `.rpm`)
shall install all components into a configurable prefix, register
the license daemon, and run a post-install smoke test.

- Acceptance: fresh-host install on each supported distro completes in <= 5 minutes and passes the smoke test.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-702 - Dependency footprint

The installer shall declare all external runtime dependencies.
Anything not in the base distro must be bundled.

- Acceptance: dependency audit passes; no surprise yum/apt requirements at runtime.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-703 - Upgrade in place

A version N+1 installer over version N shall preserve config,
license, and existing checkpoints; report any incompatibilities
explicitly.

- Acceptance: N -> N+1 upgrade test on each supported distro; checkpoints from N work on N+1 or produce a documented error.
- Traces: MR-G, MRD section 8

### FR-704 - Uninstaller

Clean uninstall shall remove all installed files, license records,
and daemons. User-generated data (reports, checkpoints) preserved
unless explicitly removed.

- Acceptance: post-uninstall, no `hsim` binaries on path; no daemons running.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-705 - Documentation set

Shipped with installer:
- Installation guide
- User guide (mirrors `docs/USER_GUIDE.md`)
- ABI reference (`hybrid_state_v1`, trigger spec, report schema)
- Integration guide (CI, Python API)
- Limitations document (current envelope from `limitation.md`)
- Error code reference (from FR-605)
- Release notes per version

- Acceptance: documentation review by an external technical writer signs off readability.
- Traces: MRD section 8.4

---

## 10. FR-8xx Support & Lifecycle

### FR-801 - Versioning

Semantic versioning: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. ABI breaks bump MAJOR.

- Acceptance: version policy documented; any ABI break is gated by a code review checklist.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-802 - Support tiers

| Tier | Response | Channels |
|---|---|---|
| Standard | 3 business days | email, web ticket |
| Premium | 1 business day | email, web ticket, named FAE |
| Mission Critical | 4 hours | phone, dedicated FAE, war-room access |

- Acceptance: each tier has a documented SLA and escalation path.
- Traces: MRD section 6.1

### FR-803 - EOL policy

Each MAJOR version shall be supported for >= 3 years from GA; EOL
announced >= 12 months in advance.

- Acceptance: EOL policy published; reflected in license terms.
- Traces: MRD section 8

### FR-804 - Patch release cadence

PATCH releases every 4 weeks for v1.0; MINOR releases every quarter.

- Acceptance: release cadence documented and trackable in CI.
- Traces: MRD section 8.2

---

## 11. FR-9xx Security & Compliance

### FR-901 - License server security

The license daemon shall:
- TLS 1.3 for all network communication
- HSM-bound private keys
- Logged audit trail of every check-out / check-in

- Acceptance: third-party security audit; OWASP Top 10 review.
- Traces: MRD section 6.2

### FR-902 - Open-source compliance

For every OSS component shipped, the installer shall include:
- License text
- Source pointer (URL or escrow)
- Modification disclosure (for LGPL components like Verilator)

- Acceptance: OSS compliance audit by Andes legal.
- Traces: MRD section 10 (Verilator licensing review)

### FR-903 - Export control

Product classification reviewed for US EAR / ITAR; documented ECCN.
Installer enforces destination country checks where required.

- Acceptance: export control review by Andes legal; ECCN documented in product sheet.
- Traces: MRD section 6.3

### FR-904 - Supply chain integrity

All shipped binaries shall be signed with an Andes code-signing
certificate. Installer verifies signatures before extraction.

- Acceptance: signature verification on every install; tampered installer is refused with a clear message.
- Traces: MR-D, MR-K

---

Mapping FR to test suites. Each test suite is owned by a named
engineer; pass/fail tracked in CI dashboard before any release.

| Suite | Covers | Owner |

| smoke | FR-101, FR-204, FR-701, FR-702 | tbd |

| trace | FR-111, FR-112 | tbd |
| determinism | FR-604, FR-203 | tbd |
| license | FR-504, FR-505, FR-506 | tbd |
| ip-protection | FR-501, FR-502, FR-503 | tbd |
| installer | FR-701, FR-702, FR-703, FR-704 | tbd |
| docs | FR-705 | tbd |
| security | FR-901, FR-902, FR-903, FR-904 | tbd |

| MR-A | Cycle-exact ROI on customer workloads | FR-101, FR-102, FR-103, FR-106, FR-108, FR-202, FR-404 |
| MR-B | Linux + userspace ROI | FR-109 |

Every MR has at least 2 supporting FRs. Every FR traces back to
at least one MR. No orphan requirements.

---

## 14. Open Engineering Questions

For Engineering / IP officer review:

- **Encryption mechanism**: in-house obfuscation pass on Verilator
  output, or external Carbon-style partner? Trade-off:
  build-vs-buy, royalty vs salary, time-to-market.
- **License daemon**: build on FlexLM (industry standard but
  licensing fee), Reprise RLM, or in-house? FlexLM has highest
  customer acceptance.
- **State-transport encryption key**: derive from license daemon
  on each run, or fixed per install? Per-run is more secure but
  adds latency.
- **vsim binary size**: encrypted output is typically 2-5x source
  size; what is the acceptable footprint?
- **Multi-hart determinism**: scheduling order in vsim cycle engine
  is deterministic given seed; QEMU side may not be. Strategy?
- **Vendor CSR list**: FR-401 says "published in AndeStar V5"; need
  a frozen list per core for the v1.0 commit.
- **Source escrow**: which neutral agent (Iron Mountain, NCC, etc)
  and what are the customer-facing trigger conditions?

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/limitation.md`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

1	# Hybrid Simulator - Current Limitations
2	
3	What this simulator cannot do today, and where it will give wrong answers,
4	hang, or crash on a real workload. Written 2026-05-28 from a direct read of
5	the current code (not just the older audit notes).
6	
7	How this file relates to the others:
8	
9	- `ROADMAP.md` (top level) - the master feature roadmap. Every open
10	  limitation below is absorbed there as an `F-ENG-*` feature; that file is
11	  the *plan to fix*. This file stays the *plain-English "do not do this"
12	  list* and the source of the L-ids.
13	- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - the older failure-mode backlog (`F-T*`) and the
14	  gem5-parity bug-audit wave (`B1-B20`, fully closed), both superseded by
15	  `ROADMAP.md`. Kept for history.
16	
17	Each entry below was checked against the code on 2026-05-28. The `Where`
18	line points at the exact file and line that proves the limit.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## The core rule: the vsim measurement window (ROI) is very narrow
23	
24	This is the single most important limitation. Everything in Tier 1 is a
25	consequence of it.
26	
27	When execution hands off to vsim, the resume step writes back only a small
28	part of the CPU state. Read `resume_driver.hpp:60-145`: it restores GPRs,
29	FPRs, the V registers, PC, and only four CSRs - `mstatus`, `mtvec`,
30	`mcycle`, `minstret`. It does NOT write `satp`, `mepc`, `mcause`, `mtval`,
31	`mscratch`, `medeleg`, `mideleg`, `mip`, `mie`, or any PMP register.
32	
33	So the region you measure on vsim (between `enter_vsim` and `exit_vsim`) MUST
34	be:
35	
36	- M-mode only (no S-mode, no U-mode)
37	- No virtual memory / paging (satp is at reset = bare mode)
38	- Trap-free (no exceptions, no interrupts, no ebreak)
39	- PMP-static (no memory-protection setup is carried in)
40	- No system calls / semihosting
41	- No atomics that cross the handoff boundary
42	- No MMIO (UART, PLIC, timer, ROM)
43	
44	If the measured region steps outside this envelope, the result is silently
45	wrong or the run hangs. Each case is listed below.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## State coverage: what the wire format carries
50	
51	Inventory view of the ROI rule above. Everything below is checked against
52	`include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (struct), the QEMU plugin drain
53	(`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`), the vsim resume (`resume_driver.hpp`),
54	the vsim drain (`state_drain.hpp`), and the QEMU2 handback
55	(`tools/orchestrator/gdbstub.py`).
56	
57	### Carried in `hybrid_state_v1`
58	
59	- 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs
60	- 13 M-mode CSRs: `mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch,
61	  medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp`
62	- PMP: 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
63	- V extension: `vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, vreg[32], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr`
64	- F13 warmup metadata: `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`
65	- `reserved[216]` = room for ~27 more `uint64` before a v2 layout is needed
66	
67	### NOT in the wire format at all
68	
69	- All S-mode CSRs: `stvec, sepc, scause, stval, sscratch, sie, sip,
70	  scounteren, senvcfg, stimecmp`
71	- `fcsr / frm / fflags` (FP rounding mode + sticky flags). See L20.
72	- HPM block: `mhpmcounter3..31`, `mhpmevent3..31`, `mcounteren,
73	  menvcfg, mcountinhibit, mconfigptr, misa, time`
74	- Every Andes-custom CSR (`mmsc_cfg, mcache_ctl, mmisc_ctl, micm_cfg,
75	  mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec`, ...). See L21.
76	
77	### Carried but NOT restored into vsim
78	
79	The struct holds them so they survive QEMU1 -> QEMU2, but `ResumeDriver`
80	writes none of them into the vsim hart. They are dead during the ROI:
81	
82	- `satp` (L3), `mepc / mcause / mtval` (L4), `mscratch, medeleg,
83	  mideleg, mip, mie`, and all PMP (L2).
84	
85	Only four CSRs are actually restored into vsim: `mstatus, mtvec,
86	mcycle, minstret` (`resume_driver.hpp:60-145`).
87	
88	### Transport ceiling - why "all CSRs" is not free
89	
90	Four surfaces, four ceilings:
91	
92	| Surface         | Mechanism                                     | Ceiling |
93	|-----------------|-----------------------------------------------|---------|
94	| QEMU1 drain     | plugin reads by NAME from gdbstub XML         | only CSRs the QEMU fork advertises |
95	| vsim resume     | DMI Abstract Cmd + Program Buffer (by number) | RO / WARL / locked bits will not take arbitrary values |
96	| vsim drain      | DMI Abstract read (by number)                 | general for any readable CSR |
97	| QEMU2 handback  | gdbstub P-packet by NAME                      | silently skipped if stub omits the name (L16); `vl / vtype` already needed a QEMU fork patch |
98	
99	Two structural blockers to "all CSRs":
100	
101	1. Wire format is a fixed C struct; `reserved[216]` fits about 27 more
102	   `uint64`. Reaching the full M + S + HPM + Andes set needs a v2 layout.
103	2. Semantics, not just bits. Restore order and side effects already bite
104	   (`mstatus.FS/VS` gating, `vsetvl` atomicity for `vtype/vl`). Writing
105	   `satp` flushes the TLB; Andes `mcache_ctl / mmisc_ctl` toggle caches,
106	   prefetchers, branch prediction and may be RO or locked when written
107	   via the debug module mid-run. Those are exactly the CSRs that shape
108	   the cycle figure.
109	
110	Verdict: extending the wire format to a bounded set (`fcsr`, S-mode trap
111	CSRs, a chosen Andes microarch subset) in a v2 layout is feasible.
112	"All RISC-V CSRs including Andes-specific" is not feasible without
113	redesigning the wire format and lifting the entire ROI envelope (L2-L6).
114

116	
117	## Tier 1 - Will break on the next real workload
118	
119	### L1. No system calls / semihosting inside the ROI  (F-T1.1)
120	
121	- When it bites: any C code calling `printf`, `malloc`, `_exit`, `fopen`, or
122	  anything that ends up in `libgloss` between `enter_vsim()` and `exit_vsim()`.
123	- What happens: libgloss emits the semihosting magic triple
124	  (`slli x0,x0,0x1f; ebreak; srai x0,x0,0x7`). vsim has no semihosting
125	  handler, so the ebreak traps, the trap handler calls `_exit`, which is
126	  another ebreak -> infinite trap loop -> the run times out.
127	- Where: `docs/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md` (unsolved);
128	  `tests/fixtures/runtime/{trap.S,handler.c}`.
129	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: keep all I/O in phase 1 / phase 3 (the two QEMU
130	  legs). Do not put any syscall in the measured region.
131	
132	### L2. PMP protection is not carried into vsim  (F-T1.3)
133	
134	- When it bites: a workload that relies on PMP-enforced memory regions
135	  (write-protect, execute-lock) inside the ROI.
136	- What happens: the QEMU plugin drains all 16 `pmpcfg` + 64 `pmpaddr`
137	  entries (`hybrid_handoff.c:292-295`), but the resume step writes none of
138	  them. vsim runs the ROI with zeroed PMP, so any protection from phase 1
139	  silently disappears. (PMP IS restored to QEMU2 afterward, so the gap is
140	  the vsim window only.)
141	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp` - no `pmpcfg`/`pmpaddr` write path exists.
142	- Status: OPEN.
143	
144	### L3. Virtual memory (paging) is off inside the ROI
145	
146	- When it bites: any workload running with paging enabled (satp != 0), i.e.
147	  almost anything under an OS.
148	- What happens: `satp` is drained and restored to QEMU2, but the resume step
149	  never writes `satp` into vsim. The ROI executes in bare mode, so every
150	  virtual address is treated as physical. Loads/stores hit the wrong memory.
151	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp:32-42` (CSR constant list has no satp);
152	  `resume()` never writes it.
153	- Status: OPEN, and only partly documented (CLAUDE.md mentions trap-free +
154	  PMP-static but not paging).
155	
156	### L4. Trap / exception state is lost across the ROI  (F-T1.4)
157	
158	- When it bites: any trap (illegal instruction, page fault, misaligned
159	  access, ebreak) fires inside the ROI.
160	- What happens: at drain, `mcause`, `mtval`, `mepc` are NOT re-read from
161	  vsim; the stale QEMU1 values pass straight through to QEMU2. Any
162	  trap-diagnostic logic after the handoff sees wrong values. Also `mepc`/
163	  trap-delegation CSRs are not restored into vsim, so trap handling inside
164	  the ROI starts from reset values.
165	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:71-109` (`drain_with_passthrough` re-reads GPRs,
166	  FPRs, V-CSRs, mcycle, minstret - but not mcause/mtval/mepc).
167	- Status: OPEN.
168	
169	### L5. Atomics (LR/SC) cannot cross the handoff  (F-T1.5)
170	
171	- When it bites: an `lr.{w,d}` retires before the trigger and the matching
172	  `sc.{w,d}` retires after it - or any reservation held across the boundary.
173	- What happens: the LR/SC reservation is not part of the wire format, so it
174	  never round-trips. The `sc` always fails on re-entry; a
175	  `__atomic_compare_exchange` loop spins forever.
176	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` - no reservation field.
177	- Status: OPEN. The plan is to reject (not transport) a pending reservation
178	  at the trigger.
179	
180	### L20. FP rounding mode (fcsr) does not round-trip  (new 2026-05-28)
181	
182	- When it bites: any workload that sets a non-default rounding mode
183	  (`frm != 0 / RNE`) before the ROI, or relies on sticky `fflags` after
184	  it, while running FP code inside.
185	- What happens: `fcsr` (which packs `frm[7:5]` and `fflags[4:0]`) is not
186	  in `hybrid_state_v1`. The plugin does not drain it; the resume step
187	  does not restore it; the drain does not read it back. vsim sees the
188	  reset value (RNE, no flags); QEMU2 keeps QEMU1's pre-trigger value
189	  with no sync. FP results inside the ROI use the wrong rounding;
190	  sticky flags after the ROI are wrong.
191	- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (no `fcsr` field);
192	  `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (no `fcsr` handle in `VcpuRegs`);
193	  `resume_driver.hpp` (no `fcsr` restore).
194	- Status: OPEN. Concrete next move: add `uint64_t fcsr` from
195	  `reserved[]`, drain alongside FPRs, restore after `mstatus.FS` is
196	  enabled, drain before handback.
197

200	## Tier 2 - Will break when you scale up
201	
202	### L6. Whole-program (S/U-mode) privilege is forced to M-mode  (F-T2.1)
203	
204	- When it bites: a kernel/Linux-style workload that is in S- or U-mode at the
205	  trigger boundary.
206	- What happens: both sides hardcode `priv = 3` (M-mode):
207	  `state_drain.hpp:51` and `hybrid_handoff.c:264`. On the vsim side DCSR.prv
208	  is never written, so `dret` always resumes in M-mode. On the QEMU2 side,
209	  `apply_state` never writes `priv` at all (it is in the struct at
210	  `abi.py:37` but absent from `gdbstub.py:271-319`). S/U code then raises
211	  illegal-instruction -> trap loop.
212	- Where: `state_drain.hpp:51`, `hybrid_handoff.c:264`, `gdbstub.py` apply_state.
213	- Status: OPEN.
214	
215	### L7. Workload must fit in the 128 MB shared mmap, with no bounds check  (F-T2.2)
216	
217	- When it bites: heap, stack, or static data extends past the default 128 MB
218	  shared memory.
219	- What happens: there is no startup check that the ELF segments fit. vsim's
220	  memory rejects or truncates the access; QEMU may see it as MMIO. Silent
221	  corruption.
222	- Where: orchestrator mmap sizing; `--mmap-size` exists but nothing validates
223	  ELF size against it.
224	- Status: OPEN. Workaround: pass `--mmap-size` large enough by hand.
225	
226	### L8. Single hart only  (F-T2.3)
227	
228	- When it bites: any multi-hart config (`_NDS_NHART=2`), IPIs, hart-to-hart
229	  sync.
230	- What happens: the resume/drain code only handles hart 0. The icount
231	  counter is a single `uint64_t` (`icount_trigger.hpp:14-15`); BBV emit is
232	  single-hart (`bbv_emit.h:9`). Resuming hart 1 from hart 0 state corrupts
233	  both.
234	- Where: `resume_driver.hpp`, `state_drain.hpp`, `icount_trigger.hpp:14`,
235	  `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h:9`.
236	- Status: OPEN.
237	
238	### L9. MMIO inside the ROI is not handled  (F-T2.5)
239	
240	- When it bites: the ROI touches UART (`putchar`), PLIC, the timer, ROM, or
241	  any aliased/device memory.
242	- What happens: the Phase-5 interconnect watch was never built. Writes to
243	  MMIO ranges either vanish or hit RAM as if they were normal memory. QEMU2
244	  device state then disagrees with vsim.
245	- Where: no allowlist/watch in the platform interconnect.
246	- Status: OPEN.
247
